How to read this report: Sections 1–7 describe the GWAS harmonization and preprocessing pipeline, while sections executed with live evaluation (eval = TRUE) — notably 8, 9, 11–12, and 14–19 — present diagnostic outputs, causal results, and machine-learning feature screening derived from the harmonized data.



Purpose of the workflow

This report documents the standardized ingestion, harmonization, and quality control of multiple GWAS summary-statistics datasets spanning accelerometry-derived physical activity traits, biological predictors, and aging-related outcomes. The primary objective is to construct two fully aligned analysis matrices:

a SNP × trait effect size matrix for Elastic Net machine-learning modeling, and

a long-format GWAS table optimized for two-sample Mendelian Randomization analyses.

Sections 1–3 are executed with live evaluation (eval = TRUE) to establish the computational environment, automatically discover all GWAS inputs, standardize heterogeneous column formats, and define biologically meaningful trait mappings required for downstream processing.

From Section 4 onward, the workflow implements the core harmonization and quality control pipeline, including accelerometry-based SNP universe construction, CHR:BP → rsID mapping, global SNP intersection, duplicate control, integrity audits, and generation of final modeling matrices. Several of these steps are computationally intensive and therefore configured with eval = FALSE once validated. To ensure reproducibility without repeated heavy computation, key intermediate and final datasets are cached to disk as RDS files, including:

accel_reference_snps.rds — shared accelerometry SNP universe

gwas_list_final.rds — fully harmonized GWAS traits aligned to the common SNP set

X_elastic_net.rds — full SNP × trait effect size matrix

gwas_mr.rds — long-format MR-ready dataset

These saved objects are reloaded in later sections to support validation, visualization, causal inference, and machine-learning analyses without rerunning the entire preprocessing pipeline.

The primary analytical results are presented in sections executed with live evaluation (eval = TRUE), specifically:

Section 8 — post-harmonization sanity checks and effect size diagnostics

Section 9 — MR field availability audits

Section 11 — MR input integrity diagnostics

Section 12 — exhaustive SNP harmonization validation

Section 14 — reloading and reproducible restoration of MR result objects

Section 15 — Mendelian Randomization causal estimates and sensitivity visualizations

Section 16 — SNP dimensionality reduction for Elastic Net modeling

Section 17 — SNP-level genetic correlation screening

Section 18 — univariate SNP-level regression screening

Section 19 — integrated predictor prioritization across methods

Together, this workflow delivers a rigorously harmonized genetic dataset, efficient reuse of large-scale intermediate objects, and a transparent results framework connecting causal inference and machine-learning approaches to characterize shared genetic architecture underlying human aging outcomes.

# 2. Robust GWAS Reader and Column Standardization

This section defines a flexible, memory-efficient GWAS reader capable of harmonizing heterogeneous summary-statistics formats. It standardizes SNP identifiers, alleles, effect sizes, standard errors, and allele frequencies across studies, while supporting both rsID and CHR:BP SNP formats.

## 2.1 Memory-efficient GWAS loading and column harmonization function


```{r load_GWAS2, echo=TRUE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=TRUE}

#============================================================
# 3. Robust reader helpers (UNCHANGED logic, but reusable)
#============================================================

# Define column aliases based on your audit
col_aliases <- list(
  SNP  = c("RSID","rsid","rs_id","variant_id","SNP","SNPID","snpid"),
  EA   = c("effect_allele","EA","A1","a1","ALLELE1","Allele1","ALT"),
  OA   = c("other_allele","OA","A2","a0","ALLELE0","Allele2","REF"),
  BETA = c("beta","BETA","effect","beta1","Effect"),
  SE   = c("standard_error","SE","se","StdErr"),
  EAF  = c("effect_allele_frequency","EAF","A1FREQ","freq1","Freq1","AF","MAF")
)


read_gwas_4cols <- function(f) {

  # Read header only
  cols <- strsplit(readLines(f, n = 1), "[\t ]+")[[1]]

  # Identify matching columns
  selected <- lapply(col_aliases, function(x) intersect(x, cols)[1])

  has_snp  <- !is.na(selected$SNP)
  has_beta <- !is.na(selected$BETA)

  # Allow CHR+BP instead of SNP
  chr_alias <- c("chromosome","CHR","chr","CHROM")
  bp_alias  <- c("base_pair_location","BP","pos","POS","position")

  has_chr <- any(chr_alias %in% cols)
  has_bp  <- any(bp_alias %in% cols)

  has_chr_bp <- has_chr & has_bp


  if (!has_beta) {
    stop(
      "Missing BETA column in file: ", basename(f), "\n",
      "Detected columns: ", paste(cols, collapse = ", ")
    )
  }

  if (!has_snp && !has_chr_bp) {
    stop(
      "Missing SNP and CHR/BP columns in file: ", basename(f), "\n",
      "Detected columns: ", paste(cols, collapse = ", ")
    )
  }

  # Columns to read
  read_cols <- unname(unlist(selected[c("SNP", "EA", "OA", "BETA", "SE", "EAF")]))
  read_cols <- read_cols[!is.na(read_cols)]

  # Also read chr/bp if SNP missing
  if (!has_snp && has_chr_bp) {
    read_cols <- unique(c(read_cols, "chromosome", "base_pair_location"))
  }

  # Read file (memory-safe)
  df <- fread(
    cmd = paste("cmd /c type", shQuote(normalizePath(f, winslash = "\\"))),
    select = read_cols,
    showProgress = FALSE
  )

  # Rename known columns
  rename_map <- unlist(selected[!is.na(selected)], use.names = TRUE)

  setnames(
    df,
    old = unname(rename_map),
    new = names(rename_map),
    skip_absent = TRUE
  )

  # Construct SNP if needed
  if (!"SNP" %in% names(df) && has_chr_bp) {
    df[, SNP := paste0(chromosome, ":", base_pair_location)]
  }

  # Ensure allele columns exist
  if (!"EA" %in% names(df)) df[, EA := NA_character_]
  if (!"OA" %in% names(df)) df[, OA := NA_character_]

  # Keep final structure (now includes SE and EAF if present)
  keep_cols <- c("SNP", "EA", "OA", "BETA", "SE", "EAF")
  keep_cols <- intersect(keep_cols, names(df))

  df <- df[, ..keep_cols]

  return(df)
}



```

# 4. Accelerometry Reference SNP Universe Construction

Accelerometry GWAS traits are loaded first to define a high-quality, shared SNP reference universe. Because all accelerometry traits originate from the same UK Biobank GWAS framework, a single trait is sufficient to establish the full SNP panel.

## 4.1 Loading accelerometry GWAS and defining the common SNP reference panel

All accelerometry GWAS files are harmonized and verified to share identical SNP sets. This SNP list is saved as a reusable reference panel that anchors all subsequent cross-trait harmonization.

# 5. SNP Format Audit and Harmonization

Before large-scale integration, SNP identifier formats across all GWAS files are audited to detect rsID versus CHR:BP usage. This pre-flight step prevents silent mismatches and guides the required mapping strategy.

## 5.1 Pre-flight SNP identifier format detection

Representative rows from each GWAS file are scanned to quantify rsID and CHR:BP usage, flagging datasets requiring coordinate-to-rsID conversion prior to joint analysis.

```{r load_GWAS4.1, echo=TRUE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=TRUE}


#============================================================
# 5B. PRE-FLIGHT SNP FORMAT CHECK
#     - 1 PA reference file
#     - all non-PA traits
#============================================================

check_snp_format_fast <- function(f, group, n = 100) {

  lines <- tryCatch(readLines(f, n = n), error = function(e) NULL)

  if (is.null(lines) || length(lines) < 2) {
    return(data.frame(
      file = basename(f),
      group = group,
      snp_type = "READ_ERROR",
      rsID_pct = NA_real_,
      chr_bp_pct = NA_real_
    ))
  }

  # Parse header
  header <- strsplit(lines[1], "[\t ]+")[[1]]

  snp_col   <- intersect(c("RSID","rsid","rs_id","SNP","variant_id","SNPID"), header)
  has_chr_bp <- all(c("chromosome", "base_pair_location") %in% header)

  # Parse first data rows
  data <- strsplit(lines[-1], "[\t ]+")
  df <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, data), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  names(df) <- header[seq_len(ncol(df))]

  # Extract SNPs
  if (length(snp_col) > 0 && snp_col[1] %in% names(df)) {
    snp <- df[[snp_col[1]]]
  } else if (has_chr_bp) {
    snp <- paste0(df$chromosome, ":", df$base_pair_location)
  } else {
    return(data.frame(
      file = basename(f),
      group = group,
      snp_type = "UNKNOWN",
      rsID_pct = NA_real_,
      chr_bp_pct = NA_real_
    ))
  }

  rs_pct  <- mean(grepl("^rs[0-9]+$", snp))
  chr_pct <- mean(grepl("^[0-9]+:[0-9]+$", snp))

  data.frame(
    file = basename(f),
    group = group,
    snp_type = ifelse(rs_pct > 0.5, "rsID", "CHR:BP"),
    rsID_pct = round(rs_pct, 3),
    chr_bp_pct = round(chr_pct, 3)
  )
}

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Run pre-flight
#------------------------------------------------------------

# Use ONE PA file as reference (all PA share same SNPs)
pa_ref_file <- files_accel[1]

snp_format_preflight <- rbind(
  check_snp_format_fast(pa_ref_file, group = "PA_reference"),
  do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(files_other, check_snp_format_fast, group = "Other")
  )
)
```

# 6. Global SNP Harmonization and Quality Control

All GWAS datasets are harmonized onto the accelerometry SNP universe through fast CHR:BP → rsID mapping, global SNP intersection, and duplicate removal. This produces a fully aligned multi-trait GWAS collection with one effect estimate per SNP per trait.

## 6.1 CHR:BP to rsID mapping and cross-trait SNP alignment

Non-PA GWAS traits using coordinate-based SNPs are converted to rsIDs using a reference lookup derived from accelerometry GWAS. All traits are restricted to the shared SNP universe, intersected across datasets, and rigorously deduplicated.


```{r load_GWAS4.2, echo=TRUE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=FALSE}


#============================================================
# SECTION 6 — Memory-Safe Global SNP Harmonization
#============================================================

library(data.table)
options(datatable.fread.mmap = FALSE)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# 6.0 Create organized output folders
#------------------------------------------------------------

mapped_dir <- file.path(out_dir, "mapped_full_traits")
final_dir  <- file.path(out_dir, "final_harmonized_traits")

if (!dir.exists(mapped_dir)) dir.create(mapped_dir)
if (!dir.exists(final_dir))  dir.create(final_dir)

cat("📁 Output folders ready\n")


#------------------------------------------------------------
# 6.1 Build PA CHR:BP → rsID lookup (RUN ONLY ONCE)
#------------------------------------------------------------

# ONE PA file is sufficient (all PA traits share SNP universe)
pa_ref_file <- files_accel[1]

pa_lookup <- fread(
  pa_ref_file,
  select = c("variant_id", "chromosome", "base_pair_location"),
  showProgress = FALSE
)

# Build CHR:BP key
pa_lookup[, chr_bp := paste0(chromosome, ":", base_pair_location)]

# variant_id is rsID in UKB PA GWAS
setnames(pa_lookup, "variant_id", "rsID")

# Keep minimal lookup
pa_lookup <- unique(pa_lookup[, .(chr_bp, rsID)])

# Key for fast joins
setkey(pa_lookup, chr_bp)

cat("✅ PA lookup built with",
    nrow(pa_lookup), "CHR:BP → rsID mappings\n")


#------------------------------------------------------------
# 6.2 Sequential Trait Mapping (Memory Safe)
#------------------------------------------------------------

processed_trait_files <- c()

for (i in seq_along(files_other)) {

  f <- files_other[i]
  trait_name <- trait_mapping[basename(f)]

  cat("🔄 Processing:", trait_name, "\n")

  df <- read_gwas_4cols(f)
  
  
  # Fix rsID:REF:ALT format
  if (mean(grepl("^rs[0-9]+:[A-Za-z]:[A-Za-z]$", df$SNP)) > 0.5) {
    df[, SNP := sub(":.*", "", SNP)]
  }

  # Detect CHR:BP format
  if (mean(grepl("^rs[0-9]+$", df$SNP)) < 0.5) {

    setnames(df, "SNP", "chr_bp")

    df <- pa_lookup[df, nomatch = 0]

    setnames(df, "rsID", "SNP")

    df[, chr_bp := NULL]
  }

  # Remove duplicated SNPs immediately
  df <- df[!duplicated(df$SNP), ]

  out_file <- file.path(
    mapped_dir,
    paste0("mapped_full_", trait_name, ".rds")
  )

  saveRDS(df, out_file)

  processed_trait_files <- c(processed_trait_files, out_file)

  rm(df)
  gc(TRUE)
}

cat("✅ All traits mapped and saved individually\n")



#------------------------------------------------------------
# 6.2.1 WHR_adjBMI management
#------------------------------------------------------------

library(data.table)

# 1️⃣ Identify file
f <- files_other[basename(files_other) == "GCST008999_WHRadjBMI.tbl"]
trait_name <- "WHR_adjBMI"

cat("🔧 Reprocessing:", trait_name, "\n")

# 2️⃣ Read using your normal reader
df <- read_gwas_4cols(f)

# 3️⃣ FIX rsID format (remove allele suffix)
df[, SNP := sub(":.*", "", SNP)]

# 4️⃣ Remove duplicates
df <- df[!duplicated(df$SNP), ]

# 5️⃣ Save corrected mapped file (overwrite)
out_file <- file.path(
  mapped_dir,
  paste0("mapped_full_", trait_name, ".rds")
)

saveRDS(df, out_file)

rm(df)
gc(TRUE)

cat("✅ WHR_adjBMI reprocessed and overwritten\n")



#------------------------------------------------------------
# 6.3 Compute Global SNP Intersection (Disk Streaming)
#------------------------------------------------------------

common_file <- file.path(out_dir, "common_snps_universe.rds")

if (!file.exists(common_file)) {

  cat("🔎 Computing global SNP intersection...\n")

  common_snps <- NULL

  for (f in processed_trait_files) {

    df <- readRDS(f)

    if (is.null(common_snps)) {
      common_snps <- df$SNP
    } else {
      common_snps <- intersect(common_snps, df$SNP)
    }

    rm(df)
    gc(FALSE)
  }

  saveRDS(common_snps, common_file)

  cat("✅ Common SNP universe saved\n")

} else {

  cat("📦 Loading existing common SNP universe\n")
}

common_snps <- readRDS(common_file)

cat("📊 Total common SNPs:", length(common_snps), "\n")


#------------------------------------------------------------
# 6.4 Restrict Each Trait to Final SNP Universe
#------------------------------------------------------------

final_trait_files <- c()

for (f in processed_trait_files) {

  trait_name <- gsub("mapped_full_|\\.rds", "", basename(f))

  cat("🔒 Restricting:", trait_name, "\n")

  df <- readRDS(f)

  df <- df[df$SNP %in% common_snps, ]

  final_file <- file.path(
    final_dir,
    paste0("final_", trait_name, ".rds")
  )

  saveRDS(df, final_file)

  final_trait_files <- c(final_trait_files, final_file)

  rm(df)
  gc(TRUE)
}

cat("✅ Final harmonized traits saved individually\n")


#------------------------------------------------------------
# 6.5 (Optional) Build Combined Object Only If Needed
#------------------------------------------------------------

# WARNING: This loads everything into memory.
# Only run if absolutely necessary.

gwas_list_final <- lapply(final_trait_files, readRDS)
names(gwas_list_final) <- gsub("final_|\\.rds", "", basename(final_trait_files))
saveRDS(gwas_list_final, file.path(out_dir, "gwas_list_final.rds"))
rm(gwas_list_final)
gc(TRUE)

cat("🚀 SECTION 6 COMPLETE — Memory-safe harmonization finished\n")

    full.names = TRUE
  )[1]

  if (is.na(raw_file) || length(raw_file) == 0) {
    return(data.table(
      trait = trait,
      raw_snps = NA_integer_,
      mapped_snps = nrow(readRDS(mapped_path)),
      retained_pct = NA_real_
    ))
  }

  # ---- Count raw rows without loading whole file ----
  raw_n <- tryCatch(
    nrow(fread(raw_file, select = 1)),
    error = function(e) NA_integer_
  )

  mapped_n <- nrow(readRDS(mapped_path))

  data.table(
    trait = trait,
    raw_snps = raw_n,
    mapped_snps = mapped_n,
    retained_pct = round(100 * mapped_n / raw_n, 2)
  )
})

retention_table <- rbindlist(retention_list)
retention_table[order(retained_pct)]


```

# 7. Modular Addition of New GWAS Traits

A reusable integration function is introduced to enable seamless addition of new GWAS traits while preserving SNP alignment, identifier consistency, and quality control.

## 7.1 Standardized function for incremental GWAS integration

New GWAS datasets can be loaded, SNP-mapped, restricted to the reference universe, and aligned in correct SNP order with automated QC checks, enabling scalable extension of the analysis framework.

```{r NewTraitAddition, echo=TRUE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=FALSE}


add_new_gwas_trait <- function(
  gwas_file,
  trait_name,
  accel_snps,
  pa_lookup,
  read_fun = read_gwas_4cols,
  verbose = TRUE
) {

  if (verbose) {
    cat("➕ Adding new GWAS trait:", trait_name, "\n")
  }

  #------------------------------------------------------------
  # 1. Load GWAS
  #------------------------------------------------------------
  df <- read_fun(gwas_file)

  if (verbose) {
    cat("   • Loaded", nrow(df), "rows\n")
  }

  #------------------------------------------------------------
  # 2. STANDARDIZE SNP COLUMN
  #------------------------------------------------------------

  # Priority order for rsID detection
  if ("rs_id" %in% names(df)) {
    df[, SNP := rs_id]

  } else if ("RSID" %in% names(df)) {
    df[, SNP := RSID]

  } else if ("variant_id" %in% names(df)) {
    df[, SNP := variant_id]

  } else if ("SNP" %in% names(df)) {
    df[, SNP := SNP]

  } else {
    stop("No recognizable SNP column found for ", trait_name)
  }

  #------------------------------------------------------------
  # 3. Clean rsID:REF:ALT format (e.g., rs123:T:A)
  #------------------------------------------------------------

  df[, SNP := sub(":.*", "", SNP)]

  #------------------------------------------------------------
  # 4. Detect if still not proper rsIDs
  #------------------------------------------------------------

  pct_rs <- mean(grepl("^rs[0-9]+$", df$SNP))

  if (pct_rs < 0.8) {

    if (verbose) {
      cat("   • SNPs appear to be CHR:BP → mapping to rsID\n")
    }

    # Rename temporarily
    setnames(df, "SNP", "chr_bp")

    # Join to PA lookup
    df <- pa_lookup[df, nomatch = 0]

    if (nrow(df) == 0) {
      stop("No SNPs mapped to PA universe for ", trait_name)
    }

    setnames(df, "rsID", "SNP")
    df[, chr_bp := NULL]
  }

  #------------------------------------------------------------
  # 5. Remove non-rs rows
  #------------------------------------------------------------

  df <- df[grepl("^rs[0-9]+$", SNP)]

  #------------------------------------------------------------
  # 6. Restrict to PA SNP universe
  #------------------------------------------------------------

  df <- df[df$SNP %in% accel_snps]

  if (verbose) {
    cat("   • Retained", nrow(df), "SNPs after PA restriction\n")
  }

  #------------------------------------------------------------
  # 7. Enforce SNP order
  #------------------------------------------------------------

  df <- df[match(accel_snps, df$SNP)]

  #------------------------------------------------------------
  # 8. QC checks
  #------------------------------------------------------------

  stopifnot(length(df$SNP) == length(accel_snps))
  stopifnot(identical(df$SNP, accel_snps))

  if (!"BETA" %in% names(df) && !"beta" %in% names(df)) {
    stop("BETA column missing for ", trait_name)
  }

  if (verbose) {
    cat("   ✓ SNP order aligned with PA reference\n")
    cat("   ✓ Final columns:",
        paste(names(df), collapse = ", "), "\n")
  }

  return(df)
}
```

```{r sanityChecks, echo=TRUE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Build summary table with additional QC metrics
#------------------------------------------------------------

beta_summary <- bind_rows(
  lapply(names(gwas_list_final), function(tr) {

    df <- gwas_list_final[[tr]]

    data.frame(
      trait   = tr,
      mean    = mean(df$BETA),
      sd      = sd(df$BETA),
      min     = min(df$BETA),
      max     = max(df$BETA),
      max_abs = max(abs(df$BETA))
    )
  })
)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Reference SD from accelerometry traits (baseline scale)
#------------------------------------------------------------

pa_traits <- grep(
  "^Acc_|^PA_|^LIPA|^MVPA|^Sed_|^Act_|^Dyn_|^Rel_|^L5_|^M10_",
  beta_summary$trait,
  value = TRUE
)

pa_sd_ref <- mean(beta_summary$sd[beta_summary$trait %in% pa_traits])

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Add interpretability flags
#------------------------------------------------------------

beta_summary <- beta_summary %>%
  mutate(
    sd_vs_PA = sd / pa_sd_ref,
    flag = case_when(
      max_abs > 0.5 ~ "Heavy-tailed GWAS (expected biology)",
      sd < 0.003    ~ "Low-variance trait (tight effects)",
      TRUE         ~ ""
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(sd))

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Identify rows to highlight (not errors — expected patterns)
#------------------------------------------------------------

heavy_rows <- which(beta_summary$max_abs > 0.5)
lowvar_rows <- which(beta_summary$sd < 0.003)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Render publication-grade table
#------------------------------------------------------------

tbl <- kbl(
  beta_summary,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Distribution of SNP effect sizes (BETA) per trait after harmonisation with variance diagnostics"
) %>%
  kable_styling(
    full_width = FALSE,
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover")
  )

# Highlight heavy-tailed GWAS (e.g., HDL)
for (i in heavy_rows) {
  tbl <- tbl %>% row_spec(i, background = "#FDEBD0")
}

# Highlight low-variance traits (e.g., CRF_slope)

  tbl <- tbl %>% row_spec(i, background = "#EBF5FB")
}

    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 10)

#============================================================
# Allele flip / sign concordance audit across related traits
#============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Define trait pairs and expected sign relationship
# expected = "opposite" or "same"
#------------------------------------------------------------

sign_pairs <- data.frame(
  trait_1 = c("HDL", "LDL", "Fat_mass", "CRP", "Healthspan"),
  trait_2 = c("LDL", "Triglycerides", "VAT", "WBC", "Parental_lifespan"),
  expected = c("opposite", "same", "same", "same", "same"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Compute sign concordance
#------------------------------------------------------------

sign_results <- bind_rows(
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(sign_pairs)), function(i) {

    t1 <- sign_pairs$trait_1[i]
    t2 <- sign_pairs$trait_2[i]
    expected <- sign_pairs$expected[i]

    s1 <- sign(gwas_list_final[[t1]]$BETA)
    s2 <- sign(gwas_list_final[[t2]]$BETA)

    same_dir <- s1 == s2

    pct_same <- mean(same_dir, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
    pct_opp  <- 100 - pct_same

    data.frame(
      trait_1 = t1,
      trait_2 = t2,
      expected_pattern = expected,
      percent_same_direction = round(pct_same, 2),
      percent_opposite_direction = round(pct_opp, 2),
      observed_matches_expectation = ifelse(
        (expected == "same" & pct_same > 50) |
        (expected == "opposite" & pct_opp > 50),
        "Yes",
        "Check"
      )
    )
  })
)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Render QC table
#------------------------------------------------------------

kbl(
  sign_results,
  caption = "Allele sign concordance audit across biologically related traits"
) %>%
  kable_styling(
    full_width = FALSE,
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover")
  )
```

# 9. Pre-MR Column Availability Audit and Instrument Metadata Verification

Raw GWAS files are systematically scanned to determine the availability and original naming of standard errors, allele frequencies, and sample size fields required for Mendelian Randomization analyses.

## 9.1 Detection and validation of SE, EAF, and sample size fields across GWAS files

Header-level audits identify which datasets contain SE, EAF, and N information, map original column names to standardized fields, and preview representative values to ensure numeric plausibility prior to MR modeling.


```{r MRaudit, echo=TRUE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=TRUE}


#============================================================
# PRE-MR AUDIT — Check raw files for SE / EAF / N availability
#============================================================

mr_aliases <- list(
  SE  = c("se", "SE", "stderr", "std_error", "standard_error", "sebeta"),
  EAF = c("eaf", "EAF", "effect_allele_freq", "effect_allele_frequency", "freq1", "af", "A1FREQ", "ALT_FREQ"),
  N   = c("n", "N", "samplesize", "sample_size", "N_total", "TOTAL_N", "Neff", "effective_n")
)

# helper: robust header split for tab/space-delimited files
read_header_cols <- function(f) {
  h <- readLines(f, n = 1, warn = FALSE)
  if (length(h) == 0) return(character(0))
  cols <- strsplit(h, "[\t ]+")[[1]]
  cols[cols != ""]
}

audit_one_file <- function(f) {
  cols <- read_header_cols(f)
  cols_lc <- tolower(cols)

  has <- sapply(mr_aliases, function(keys) {
    any(tolower(keys) %in% cols_lc)
  })

  # which exact matches (useful for mapping)
  matched <- lapply(names(mr_aliases), function(k) {
    keys <- tolower(mr_aliases[[k]])
    cols[tolower(cols) %in% keys]
  })
  names(matched) <- names(mr_aliases)

  data.frame(
    file = basename(f),
    has_SE  = has["SE"],
    has_EAF = has["EAF"],
    has_N   = has["N"],
    SE_cols  = ifelse(length(matched$SE)  == 0, "", paste(matched$SE,  collapse = ",")),
    EAF_cols = ifelse(length(matched$EAF) == 0, "", paste(matched$EAF, collapse = ",")),
    N_cols   = ifelse(length(matched$N)   == 0, "", paste(matched$N,   collapse = ",")),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

# Run audit on both groups
mr_audit_accel <- do.call(rbind, lapply(files_accel, audit_one_file))
mr_audit_other <- do.call(rbind, lapply(files_other, audit_one_file))

mr_audit <- rbind(
  transform(mr_audit_accel, group = "Accelerometry"),
  transform(mr_audit_other, group = "Other")
)

#============================================================

mr_aliases <- list(
  SE  = c("se", "SE", "stderr", "standard_error", "std_error", "sebeta"),
  EAF = c("eaf", "EAF", "effect_allele_frequency", "effect_allele_freq",
          "af", "freq1", "a1freq", "alt_freq"),
  N   = c("n", "N", "samplesize", "sample_size", "neff", "total_n")
)

read_header_cols <- function(f) {
  h <- readLines(f, n = 1, warn = FALSE)
  if (length(h) == 0) return(character(0))
  cols <- strsplit(h, "[\t ]+")[[1]]
  cols[cols != ""]
}

find_original_cols <- function(f) {

  cols <- read_header_cols(f)
  cols_lc <- tolower(cols)

  find_match <- function(keys) {
    idx <- match(tolower(keys), cols_lc, nomatch = 0)
    if (all(idx == 0)) return(NA_character_)
    cols[idx[idx > 0][1]]   # return FIRST match, original name
  }

  data.frame(
    file  = basename(f),
    trait = unname(trait_mapping[basename(f)]),
    SE_col  = find_match(mr_aliases$SE),
    EAF_col = find_match(mr_aliases$EAF),
    N_col   = find_match(mr_aliases$N),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

# Run audit on all GWAS files
#------------------------------------------------------------

  rbind,
  lapply(c(files_accel, files_other), find_original_cols)

library(data.table)

preview_se_eaf <- function(f, se_col, eaf_col, n = 5) {

  cols_to_read <- na.omit(c(se_col, eaf_col))
  if (length(cols_to_read) == 0) return(data.frame())

  df <- fread(
    f,
    select = cols_to_read,
    nrows = n,
    showProgress = FALSE
  )

  # Standardize names for display
  if (!is.na(se_col) && se_col %in% names(df)) {
    setnames(df, se_col, "SE")
  }
  if (!is.na(eaf_col) && eaf_col %in% names(df)) {
    setnames(df, eaf_col, "EAF")
  }

  as.data.frame(df)
}








#============================================================
# RUN PREVIEW FOR ALL TRAITS
#============================================================

se_eaf_preview <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(mr_column_map)), function(i) {

  row <- mr_column_map[i, ]

  f <- c(files_accel, files_other)[
    basename(c(files_accel, files_other)) == row$file
  ]

  out <- preview_se_eaf(
    f      = f,
    se_col = row$SE_col,
    eaf_col = row$EAF_col,
    n = 5
  )

  if (nrow(out) == 0) return(NULL)

  out$trait <- row$trait
  out
})

names(se_eaf_preview) <- mr_column_map$trait


#============================================================
# COMBINE SE & EAF PREVIEW INTO ONE TABLE (non-PA traits)
#============================================================

  lapply(names(se_eaf_preview), function(tr) {

    df <- se_eaf_preview[[tr]]
    if (is.null(df)) return(NULL)

    df %>%
      mutate(
        trait = tr,
        SNP_row = row_number()
      ) %>%

kbl(
  se_eaf_table,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Representative SE and EAF values extracted from raw GWAS summary statistics"
) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) %>%
  scroll_box(height = "400px")







```



# 10. Construction of Analysis Matrices and Memory Optimization

Final harmonized GWAS traits are stored individually on disk and loaded only when required. A dense SNP × trait matrix is constructed for Elastic Net modeling, while Mendelian Randomization is performed trait-by-trait directly from disk without generating a global long-format object. Memory usage is minimized throughout.

## 10.1 Elastic Net Predictor Matrix Construction (Memory-Optimized)

The Elastic Net matrix is built from the final harmonized traits, aligned by the shared SNP universe. Only the required effect sizes are loaded sequentially, and no redundant global GWAS objects are retained in memory.

```{r FinalMatrixGeneration, echo=TRUE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=FALSE}


gwas_list_final <- readRDS("gwas_list_final.rds")


gwas_list_final <- lapply(gwas_list_final, function(df) {
  df[, BETA := as.numeric(BETA)]
  df
})
gc(TRUE)


#============================================================
# FINAL MATRICES IN MEMORY (NO EXCEL, NO DISK)
#============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Reference SNP order
#------------------------------------------------------------

snps <- gwas_list_final[[1]]$SNP
traits <- names(gwas_list_final)

#============================================================
# 1. ELASTIC NET MATRIX (SNPs × Traits)
#============================================================

X_elastic_net <- matrix(
  NA_real_,
  nrow = length(snps),
  ncol = length(traits),
  dimnames = list(snps, traits)
)

for (j in seq_along(traits)) {

  tr <- traits[j]
  df <- gwas_list_final[[tr]]

  # Enforce SNP order
  df <- df[match(snps, df$SNP), ]
  stopifnot(identical(df$SNP, snps))

  X_elastic_net[, j] <- df$BETA
  rm(df)
}

# Hard QC
stopifnot(!anyNA(X_elastic_net))

cat("✅ Elastic Net matrix created:",
    nrow(X_elastic_net), "SNPs ×",
    ncol(X_elastic_net), "traits\n")






#============================================================
# MEMORY AUDIT — objects ordered by size
#============================================================

obj_sizes <- sapply(ls(envir = .GlobalEnv), function(x) {
  object.size(get(x, envir = .GlobalEnv))
})

obj_sizes_df <- data.frame(
  object = names(obj_sizes),
  size_MB = as.numeric(obj_sizes) / 1024^2,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

obj_sizes_df <- obj_sizes_df[
  order(obj_sizes_df$size_MB, decreasing = TRUE),
]

print(obj_sizes_df, row.names = FALSE)







saveRDS(gwas_list_final, file = "gwas_list_final.rds")

rm(gwas_list_final)
gc(TRUE)

rm(
  accel_snps,
  pa_snps,
  common_snps,
  snps,
  snps_ref
)
gc(TRUE)


saveRDS(X_elastic_net, file = "X_elastic_net.rds")


```


# 11. MR Dataset Preprocessing and Full-SNP Integrity Validation

This section validates the harmonized GWAS datasets under two complementary analytical frameworks. For Elastic Net modeling (Section 11.1), all traits are restricted to a shared SNP universe with identical ordering and balanced representation across phenotypes to ensure matrix compatibility, numerical stability, and reproducible multivariate modeling. For Mendelian Randomization (Section 11.2), integrity checks are performed directly on the full mapped SNP sets without enforcing cross-trait equality, preserving exposure-specific genetic architecture while validating structural completeness, numeric consistency, and rsID formatting prior to instrument selection.


## 11.1 Integrity checks, allele-frequency screening, and clean Elastic Net input generation

This subsection confirms that all final harmonized GWAS traits share an identical SNP universe and consistent ordering, ensuring compatibility for dense SNP × trait matrix construction. SNP alignment, missing value audits, effect size validation, and allele-field completeness checks are performed to guarantee that the Elastic Net predictor matrix is free of structural inconsistencies before multivariate modeling.

```{r MRprecheck, echo=TRUE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=TRUE}


#============================================================
# SECTION 11.1 — Elastic Net Integrity & Harmonization Audit
# (Disk-based, memory safe)
#============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

final_dir <- file.path(out_dir, "final_harmonized_traits")

final_trait_files <- list.files(
  final_dir,
  pattern = "^final_.*\\.rds$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

trait_names <- gsub("final_|\\.rds", "", basename(final_trait_files))


############################################################
# FIX SNP ORDERING IN FINAL TRAIT FILES (ONE-TIME PATCH)
############################################################

common_snps <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, "common_snps_universe.rds"))

final_trait_files <- list.files(
  final_dir,
  pattern = "^final_.*\\.rds$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

for (f in final_trait_files) {

  df <- readRDS(f)

  # Restrict (safety) + enforce order
  df <- df[df$SNP %in% common_snps, ]
  df <- df[match(common_snps, df$SNP), ]

  stopifnot(identical(df$SNP, common_snps))

  saveRDS(df, f)

  rm(df)
}

gc(TRUE)

cat("✅ SNP ordering enforced across all final harmonized traits\n\n")



#------------------------------------------------------------
# 1️⃣ Global SNP universe consistency check
#------------------------------------------------------------

ref_df  <- readRDS(final_trait_files[1])
snps_ref <- ref_df$SNP
rm(ref_df)
gc(FALSE)

snp_consistency <- sapply(final_trait_files, function(f) {
  df <- readRDS(f)
  identical(df$SNP, snps_ref)
})

stopifnot(all(snp_consistency))

cat("✅ All traits share identical SNP universe\n")

#------------------------------------------------------------
# 2️⃣ Per-trait integrity summary (sequential, low memory)
#------------------------------------------------------------

qc_summary <- bind_rows(
  lapply(seq_along(final_trait_files), function(i) {

    df <- readRDS(final_trait_files[i])

    out <- data.frame(
      trait = trait_names[i],
      n_snps = nrow(df),
      missing_EA = sum(is.na(df$EA)),
      missing_OA = sum(is.na(df$OA)),
      missing_BETA = sum(is.na(df$BETA)),
      missing_SE = sum(is.na(df$SE)),
      missing_EAF = sum(is.na(df$EAF)),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )

    rm(df)
    gc(FALSE)

    out
  })
)

kbl(
  qc_summary,
  caption = "Integrity checks of harmonized MR-ready GWAS traits"
) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) %>%
  scroll_box(height = "400px")

#------------------------------------------------------------
# 3️⃣ Balanced SNP coverage verification
#------------------------------------------------------------

stopifnot(length(unique(qc_summary$n_snps)) == 1)

cat("✅ All traits contain",
    unique(qc_summary$n_snps),
    "SNPs\n")


############################################################
# 🔧 ONE-TIME TYPE FIX (PERMANENT)
############################################################

for (f in final_trait_files) {

  df <- readRDS(f)

  df$BETA <- as.numeric(df$BETA)
  if ("SE"  %in% names(df)) df$SE  <- as.numeric(df$SE)
  if ("EAF" %in% names(df)) df$EAF <- as.numeric(df$EAF)

  saveRDS(df, f)

  rm(df)
}

gc(TRUE)

cat("✅ Numeric types enforced in all final trait files\n\n")


#------------------------------------------------------------
# 4️⃣ Small representative preview (first 2 SNPs per trait)
#------------------------------------------------------------

preview_list <- lapply(seq_along(final_trait_files), function(i) {

  df <- readRDS(final_trait_files[i])

  out <- df[1:2, ]
  out$trait <- trait_names[i]

  rm(df)
  gc(FALSE)

  out
})

preview <- bind_rows(preview_list)

kbl(
  preview,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Representative SNP-level preview of MR input (per trait)"
) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) %>%
  scroll_box(height = "300px")

gc(TRUE)




############################################################
# 🔁 REBUILD COMBINED GWAS OBJECT (UPDATED + ORDERED)
############################################################

names(gwas_list_final) <- gsub("final_|\\.rds", "", basename(final_trait_files))

saveRDS(gwas_list_final, "gwas_list_final.rds")

rm(gwas_list_final)
gc(TRUE)

cat("✅ gwas_list_final.rds rebuilt with correct ordering and numeric types\n\n")
```

## 11.2 Integrity checks, allele-frequency screening, and clean MR input generation

This subsection validates the mapped GWAS datasets under a full SNP-universe framework suitable for trait-specific Mendelian Randomization. Unlike the Elastic Net branch, SNP equality across traits is not enforced. Instead, each trait is audited independently on disk to verify structural integrity, rsID formatting, numeric consistency of effect estimates, and exposure–outcome SNP overlap prior to instrument selection and causal inference.

The MR dataset is audited for missing alleles, effect sizes, standard errors, and allele frequencies. SNP counts per trait are verified for uniformity, and representative records are displayed to confirm successful harmonization and formatting prior to causal analysis.

```{r MRprecheck2, echo=TRUE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=TRUE}


#============================================================
# SECTION 11.X — MR Integrity Audit (Full Mapped Traits)
# Disk-based | No shared SNP universe restriction
#============================================================

library(data.table)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

mapped_dir <- file.path(out_dir, "mapped_full_traits")

mapped_trait_files <- list.files(
  mapped_dir,
  pattern = "^mapped_full_.*\\.rds$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

trait_names <- gsub("mapped_full_|\\.rds", "", basename(mapped_trait_files))

cat("🔎 Found", length(mapped_trait_files), "mapped_full traits\n\n")

#------------------------------------------------------------
# 1️⃣ Per-trait structural integrity audit
#------------------------------------------------------------

qc_summary <- bind_rows(
  lapply(seq_along(mapped_trait_files), function(i) {

    df <- readRDS(mapped_trait_files[i])

    out <- data.frame(
      trait = trait_names[i],
      n_snps = nrow(df),
      missing_SNP  = sum(is.na(df$SNP)),
      missing_EA   = sum(is.na(df$EA)),
      missing_OA   = sum(is.na(df$OA)),
      missing_BETA = sum(is.na(df$BETA)),
      missing_SE   = sum(is.na(df$SE)),
      missing_EAF  = if ("EAF" %in% names(df)) sum(is.na(df$EAF)) else NA_integer_,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )

    rm(df)
    gc(FALSE)

    out
  })
)

kbl(
  qc_summary,
  caption = "Integrity checks of mapped_full MR-ready GWAS traits (full SNP sets)"
) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) %>%
  scroll_box(height = "400px")

cat("\n✅ Structural audit complete\n\n")


#------------------------------------------------------------
# 2️⃣ Numeric type enforcement (permanent fix)
#------------------------------------------------------------

for (f in mapped_trait_files) {

  df <- readRDS(f)

  df$BETA <- as.numeric(df$BETA)
  if ("SE"  %in% names(df)) df$SE  <- as.numeric(df$SE)
  if ("EAF" %in% names(df)) df$EAF <- as.numeric(df$EAF)

  saveRDS(df, f)

  rm(df)
}

gc(TRUE)

cat("✅ Numeric types enforced across all mapped_full traits\n\n")


#------------------------------------------------------------
# 3️⃣ SNP format sanity check (must be rsIDs only)
#------------------------------------------------------------

format_check <- bind_rows(
  lapply(seq_along(mapped_trait_files), function(i) {

    df <- readRDS(mapped_trait_files[i])

    pct_rsid <- mean(grepl("^rs[0-9]+$", df$SNP)) * 100

    out <- data.frame(
      trait = trait_names[i],
      percent_valid_rsID = round(pct_rsid, 2),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )

    rm(df)
    gc(FALSE)

    out
  })
)

kbl(
  format_check,
  caption = "SNP ID format validation (rsID compliance) in mapped_full traits"
) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

cat("\n✅ SNP format audit complete\n\n")


#------------------------------------------------------------
# 4️⃣ Exposure–Outcome SNP overlap preview
# (not enforcing equality — just reporting overlap)
#------------------------------------------------------------

outcomes  <- c("Usual_walking_pace", "Parental_lifespan", "Healthspan")
exposures <- setdiff(trait_names, outcomes)

overlap_summary <- bind_rows(
  lapply(exposures, function(exp) {

    exp_df <- readRDS(file.path(mapped_dir, paste0("mapped_full_", exp, ".rds")))
    exp_snps <- exp_df$SNP

    bind_rows(
      lapply(outcomes, function(out) {

        out_df <- readRDS(file.path(mapped_dir, paste0("mapped_full_", out, ".rds")))
        out_snps <- out_df$SNP

        overlap <- length(intersect(exp_snps, out_snps))

        data.frame(
          exposure = exp,
          outcome  = out,
          snps_exposure = length(exp_snps),
          snps_outcome  = length(out_snps),
          snps_overlap  = overlap,
          overlap_percent_of_exposure =
            round(100 * overlap / length(exp_snps), 2),
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
      })
    )
  })
)

kbl(
  overlap_summary,
  caption = "Exposure–Outcome SNP overlap (full mapped SNP sets)"
) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) %>%
  scroll_box(height = "400px")

cat("\n✅ Overlap audit complete — MR ready\n\n")

gc(TRUE)



```

```{r SNPcheck, echo=TRUE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
############################################################
# 9. FAST SNP COLUMN READER (RSID OR CHR:BP SUPPORTED)
############################################################

read_raw_snps <- function(f) {

  header <- strsplit(readLines(f, n = 1), "[\t ]+")[[1]]

  # Case 1 — rsID-style SNP column
  snp_col <- intersect(
    c("SNP", "variant_id", "RSID", "rsid", "SNPID"),
    header
  )

  # Case 2 — CHR + BP format
  has_chr_bp <- all(c("chromosome", "base_pair_location") %in% header)

  if (length(snp_col) > 0) {

    df <- fread(
      f,
      select = snp_col[1],
      showProgress = FALSE
    )

    setnames(df, snp_col[1], "SNP")

    return(df$SNP)
  }

  if (has_chr_bp) {

    df <- fread(
      f,
      select = c("chromosome", "base_pair_location"),
      showProgress = FALSE
    )

    return(paste0(df$chromosome, ":", df$base_pair_location))
  }

  stop("No SNP or CHR:BP columns detected in: ", basename(f))
}


############################################################
# MINI CHR:BP → rsID LOOKUP FOR RAW VALIDATION
############################################################

pa_lookup_raw <- fread(
  pa_ref_file,
  select = c("variant_id", "chromosome", "base_pair_location"),
  showProgress = FALSE
)

pa_lookup_raw[, chr_bp := paste0(chromosome, ":", base_pair_location)]
setnames(pa_lookup_raw, "variant_id", "rsID", skip_absent=TRUE)
pa_lookup_raw <- unique(pa_lookup_raw[, .(chr_bp, rsID)])
setkey(pa_lookup_raw, chr_bp)





############################################################
# 10. OVERLAP FRACTION WITH HARMONISED SNP SET + OUTCOME OVERLAPS
############################################################
# Uses objects already defined above:
# raw_gwas_files, read_raw_snps(), pa_lookup_raw, accel_snps
############################################################
# Shows:
#  • Raw SNP count per GWAS
#  • Overlap with PA reference backbone
#  • Overlap with each aging outcome
############################################################

############################################################
# Define outcome SNP sets (used for overlap auditing)
############################################################

outcome_files <- c(
  "GCST007406-healthspan.tsv",
  "GCST009890-parental lifespan.tsv",
  "GCST90693086-usual walking pace.tsv"
)

outcome_paths <- raw_gwas_files[
  basename(raw_gwas_files) %in% outcome_files
]

outcome_snps <- lapply(outcome_paths, function(f) {

  snps <- read_raw_snps(f)

  # Map CHR:BP → rsID if needed
  if (any(grepl("^[0-9]+:[0-9]+$", snps))) {

    df_map <- data.table(chr_bp = snps)
    snps <- pa_lookup_raw[df_map, rsID, nomatch = 0]
  }

  unique(snps)
})

names(outcome_snps) <- basename(outcome_paths)

############################################################
# Combined overlap table with percentage context
############################################################

overlap_results <- lapply(raw_gwas_files, function(f) {

  raw_snps <- read_raw_snps(f)

  # Map CHR:BP to rsID if needed
  if (any(grepl("^[0-9]+:[0-9]+$", raw_snps))) {

    df_map <- data.table(chr_bp = raw_snps)
    raw_snps <- pa_lookup_raw[df_map, rsID, nomatch = 0]
  }

  raw_snps <- unique(raw_snps)

  # --- Final harmonised intersection ---
  overlap_n <- sum(snps_ref %in% raw_snps)
  overlap_frac <- overlap_n / length(snps_ref)

  # --- Outcome-specific overlaps ---
  healthspan_n <- sum(outcome_snps[["GCST007406-healthspan.tsv"]] %in% raw_snps)
  pace_n       <- sum(outcome_snps[["GCST90693086-usual walking pace.tsv"]] %in% raw_snps)
  lifespan_n   <- sum(outcome_snps[["GCST009890-parental lifespan.tsv"]] %in% raw_snps)

  data.frame(
    file = basename(f),
    raw_snps_total = length(raw_snps),

    shared_snps_present = overlap_n,
    shared_fraction = round(overlap_frac, 4),

    shared_percent = round(100 * overlap_frac, 2),

    overlap_healthspan = paste0(
      healthspan_n, " (",
      round(100 * healthspan_n / length(outcome_snps[["GCST007406-healthspan.tsv"]]), 2),
      "%)"
    ),

    overlap_walking_pace = paste0(
      pace_n, " (",
      round(100 * pace_n / length(outcome_snps[["GCST90693086-usual walking pace.tsv"]]), 2),
      "%)"
    ),

      round(100 * lifespan_n / length(outcome_snps[["GCST009890-parental lifespan.tsv"]]), 2),
      "%)"
    ),

    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
```

# 13. Paper-Ready Two-Sample Mendelian Randomization with Full Sensitivity Framework

A complete two-sample Mendelian Randomization pipeline is implemented following current best-practice guidelines, including genome-wide significant instrument selection, confounder screening using PhenoScanner-equivalent PheWAS resources, LD clumping, allele harmonization, weak-instrument filtering, and comprehensive sensitivity analyses.

## 13.1 Instrument filtering, heterogeneity-driven IVW, Steiger, leave-one-out, MR-PRESSO, and mode-based robustness

Genetic instruments are selected at genome-wide significance, screened for lifestyle and socioeconomic confounders using OpenGWAS PheWAS queries, pruned for linkage disequilibrium, and harmonized between exposures and outcomes. Causal effects are estimated using heterogeneity-adaptive IVW as the primary method alongside MR-Egger, weighted median, weighted mode, and simple mode estimators. Robustness and validity are further assessed through Steiger directionality testing, leave-one-out sensitivity analysis, and MR-PRESSO global and distortion tests for horizontal pleiotropy - outlier detection.

```{r MRpaperFinal, echo=TRUE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
#------------------------------------------------------------
# 4) Batched SNP query with progressive caching
#    - Queries only uncached SNPs
#    - Saves after each batch
#    - Stops cleanly on rate limits
#------------------------------------------------------------

query_snps_cached <- function(snps, p_cutoff = 5e-8, batch_size = 100) {

  # Identify SNPs not yet queried
  new_snps <- setdiff(snps, names(pheno_cache))

  # If all SNPs already cached, return immediately
  if (length(new_snps) == 0) {
    return(pheno_cache[snps])
  }

  message("🔎 Querying ", length(new_snps), " new SNPs (batched)")

  # Split into API-safe batches
  batches <- split(new_snps, ceiling(seq_along(new_snps) / batch_size))

  for (b in batches) {

    # Query OpenGWAS for trait associations
    res <- tryCatch(
      ieugwasr::phewas(
        variants = b,
        pval = p_cutoff
      ),
      error = function(e) {
        message("⚠️ Batch failed — saving progress and stopping")
        save_cache()
        return(NULL)
      }
    )

    # Stop cleanly if API limit reached
    if (is.null(res)) break

    # Store trait hits per SNP
    if (nrow(res) > 0) {

      split_res <- split(res$trait, res$rsid)

      for (s in b) {
        pheno_cache[[s]] <<- if (!is.null(split_res[[s]])) split_res[[s]] else character(0)
      }

    } else {

      # Explicitly store SNPs with no associations
      for (s in b) {
        pheno_cache[[s]] <<- character(0)
      }
    }

    # Save cache after each batch
    save_cache()
  }

  # Return cached trait associations for requested SNPs
  pheno_cache[snps]
}

# 5) Define lifestyle / socioeconomic confounder trait keywords

confounder_keywords <- c(
  "body mass index", "bmi",
  "smoking", "cigarette",
  "alcohol", "drinking",
  "education", "schooling",
  "income", "socioeconomic",
  "risk taking",
  "dietary", "sugar intake", "energy intake"
)


#------------------------------------------------------------
# 6) PhenoScanner-style confounder filtering of MR instruments
#    - Removes SNPs associated with lifestyle/SES traits
#    - Keeps biological-system traits intact
#------------------------------------------------------------

phenoscanner_filter_instruments <- function(inst_df) {

  # Extract instrument SNPs
  snps <- inst_df$SNP

  # Retrieve cached trait associations
  traits <- query_snps_cached(snps)

  # Identify SNPs linked to confounders
  bad_snps <- names(traits)[
    sapply(traits, function(tr) {
      if (length(tr) == 0) return(FALSE)
      any(grepl(
        paste(confounder_keywords, collapse="|"),
        tolower(tr)
      ))
    })
  ]

  # Report filtering
  if (length(bad_snps) > 0) {
    message("🧹 Removed ", length(bad_snps), " lifestyle/SES confounder SNPs")
  } else {
    message("✅ No lifestyle/SES confounder SNPs detected")
  }

  # Return cleaned instrument set
  inst_df[!inst_df$SNP %in% bad_snps, ]
}

#------------------------------------------------------------
# LD clumping (API) — disk-based trait workflow compatible
# Expects inst with columns: SNP, P
#------------------------------------------------------------
clump_instruments_api <- function(inst, kb = 10000, r2 = 0.001, pop = "EUR", batch_size = 3000) {

  if (!requireNamespace("ieugwasr", quietly = TRUE)) {
    stop("Package 'ieugwasr' not installed.")
  }

  if (nrow(inst) == 0) return(inst)

  # Split into batches to avoid 413 errors
  batches <- split(inst, ceiling(seq_len(nrow(inst)) / batch_size))

  kept_snps <- character(0)

  for (b in batches) {

    x <- data.frame(
      rsid = b$SNP,
      pval = b$P,
      id   = "exposure"
    )

    keep <- tryCatch(
      ieugwasr::ld_clump(
        x,
        clump_kb = kb,
        clump_r2 = r2,
        pop      = pop
      ),
      error = function(e) {
        message("⚠ LD clump batch failed — skipping batch")
        return(NULL)
      }
    )

    if (!is.null(keep)) {
      kept_snps <- c(kept_snps, keep$rsid)
    }
  }

  inst[inst$SNP %in% kept_snps, , drop = FALSE]
}



#------------------------------------------------------------
# Format data for TwoSampleMR (disk-based trait workflow)
# Expects df already loaded for a single trait
#------------------------------------------------------------

format_exposure_tsmr <- function(df, exp_trait, inst_snps) {

  x <- df[df$SNP %in% inst_snps,
          c("SNP", "BETA", "SE", "EAF", "EA", "OA", "P")]

  x <- data.frame(
    SNP = x$SNP,
    beta.exposure = x$BETA,
    se.exposure   = x$SE,
    eaf.exposure  = x$EAF,
    effect_allele.exposure = x$EA,
    other_allele.exposure  = x$OA,
    pval.exposure = x$P,
    id.exposure   = exp_trait,
    exposure      = exp_trait
  )

  x
}


format_outcome_tsmr <- function(df, out_trait, inst_snps) {

  y <- df[df$SNP %in% inst_snps,
          c("SNP", "BETA", "SE", "EAF", "EA", "OA", "P")]

  y <- data.frame(
    SNP = y$SNP,
    beta.outcome = y$BETA,
    se.outcome   = y$SE,
    eaf.outcome  = y$EAF,
    effect_allele.outcome = y$EA,
    other_allele.outcome  = y$OA,
    pval.outcome = y$P,
    id.outcome   = out_trait,
    outcome      = out_trait
  )

  y
}

    for (out in outcomes) {
      mr_qc[[k]] <- data.table(
        exposure = exp,
        outcome  = out,
        snps_full_matrix = n_full,
        snps_gws = 0,
        snps_after_confounder = 0,
        snps_after_clumping = 0,
        snps_after_harmonisation = 0,
        snps_after_fstat = 0,
        snps_final = 0
      )
      k <- k + 1
    }
    next
  }

  # defaults (for failed paths)
  n_after_clump <- 0
  n_after_confounder <- 0
  n_after_harmonise <- 0
  n_after_fstat <- 0
  n_final <- 0
  use_re <- NA

  inst <- inst0

  if (n_gws > 0) {

    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # 1.5) LD clumping
    #----------------------------------------------------------
    clump_file <- file.path(clump_dir, paste0("clumped_", exp, ".rds"))

    if (file.exists(clump_file)) {

  # 🔁 Load cached clumped SNPs
      inst <- readRDS(clump_file)

    } else {

      # 🚀 Run clumping once
      if (clump_mode == "api") {
        inst <- clump_instruments_api(
          inst,
          kb = 10000,
          r2 = 0.001,
          pop = pop,
          batch_size = 3000  # stable final size
        )
      }

      # 💾 Save for future runs
      saveRDS(inst, clump_file)
    }

    n_after_clump <- nrow(inst)

    if (n_after_clump == 0) {
      for (out in outcomes) {
        mr_qc[[k]] <- data.table(
          exposure = exp,
          outcome  = out,
          snps_full_matrix = n_full,
          snps_gws = n_gws,
          snps_after_confounder = 0,
          snps_after_clumping = 0,
          snps_after_harmonisation = 0,
          snps_after_fstat = 0,
          snps_final = 0
        )
        k <- k + 1
      }
      next
    }  

      #--------------------------------------------------------
      # 2) Confounder screening (FROZEN / DETERMINISTIC)
      #--------------------------------------------------------

      frozen_file <- file.path(
        frozen_dir,
        paste0(exp, "_post_confounder.rds")
      )

      if (file.exists(frozen_file)) {

        message("📦 Loading frozen instruments for ", exp)
        inst <- readRDS(frozen_file)

      } else {

        if (!(exp %in% no_phenoscanner_traits)) {

          inst <- phenoscanner_filter_instruments(inst)

        } else {

          message("⏭ Skipping PhenoScanner filtering for confounder trait: ", exp)

        }

        saveRDS(inst, frozen_file)
        message("💾 Instruments frozen for ", exp)
      }

      n_after_confounder <- nrow(inst)


      if (n_after_confounder < 3) {
        for (out in outcomes) {
          mr_qc[[k]] <- data.table(
            exposure = exp,
            outcome  = out,
            snps_full_matrix = n_full,
            snps_gws = n_gws,
            snps_after_confounder = n_after_confounder,
            snps_after_clumping = n_after_clump,
            snps_after_harmonisation = 0,
            snps_after_fstat = 0,
            snps_final = 0
          )
          k <- k + 1
        }
        next
      }

        inst_snps <- inst$SNP

        #======================================================
        # RUN ALL OUTCOMES
        #======================================================
        for (out in outcomes) {

          #----------------------------------------------------
          # 3) Format exposure/outcome GWAS
          #----------------------------------------------------
          exp_dat <- format_exposure_tsmr(exp_df, exp, inst_snps)
          
          out_df <- outcome_data[[out]]

          out_dat <- format_outcome_tsmr(out_df, out, inst_snps)

          if (nrow(exp_dat) < 3 || nrow(out_dat) < 3) {

            mr_qc[[k]] <- data.table(
              exposure = exp,
              outcome  = out,
              snps_full_matrix = n_full,
              snps_gws = n_gws,
              snps_after_confounder = n_after_confounder,
              snps_after_clumping = n_after_clump,
              snps_after_harmonisation = 0,
              snps_after_fstat = 0,
              snps_final = 0
            )

            k <- k + 1
            next
          }

          #----------------------------------------------------
          # 4) Harmonisation
          #----------------------------------------------------
          harm <- TwoSampleMR::harmonise_data(
            exposure_dat = as.data.frame(exp_dat),
            outcome_dat  = as.data.frame(out_dat),
            action = 2
          )

          harm <- harm[harm$mr_keep, , drop = FALSE]
          n_after_harmonise <- nrow(harm)

          if (n_after_harmonise < 3) {

            mr_qc[[k]] <- data.table(
              exposure = exp,
              outcome  = out,
              snps_full_matrix = n_full,
              snps_gws = n_gws,
              snps_after_confounder = n_after_confounder,
              snps_after_clumping = n_after_clump,
              snps_after_harmonisation = n_after_harmonise,
              snps_after_fstat = 0,
              snps_final = 0
            )

            k <- k + 1
            next
          }

          #----------------------------------------------------
          # 5) Weak instrument removal (F ≥ 10)
          #----------------------------------------------------
          harm$F_stat <- (harm$beta.exposure^2) / (harm$se.exposure^2)
          harm <- harm[harm$F_stat >= f_threshold, , drop = FALSE]
          n_after_fstat <- nrow(harm)

          if (n_after_fstat < 3) {

            mr_qc[[k]] <- data.table(
              exposure = exp,
              outcome  = out,
              snps_full_matrix = n_full,
              snps_gws = n_gws,
              snps_after_confounder = n_after_confounder,
              snps_after_clumping = n_after_clump,
              snps_after_harmonisation = n_after_harmonise,
              snps_after_fstat = n_after_fstat,
              snps_final = 0
            )

            k <- k + 1
            next
          }

          #----------------------------------------------------
          # 6) Reverse causation guard
          #----------------------------------------------------
          harm <- harm[harm$pval.outcome >= p_instrument, , drop = FALSE]
          n_final <- nrow(harm)

          if (n_final < 3) {

            mr_qc[[k]] <- data.table(
              exposure = exp,
              outcome  = out,
              snps_full_matrix = n_full,
              snps_gws = n_gws,
              snps_after_confounder = n_after_confounder,
              snps_after_clumping = n_after_clump,
              snps_after_harmonisation = n_after_harmonise,
              snps_after_fstat = n_after_fstat,
              snps_final = n_final
            )

            k <- k + 1
            next
          }

          #----------------------------------------------------
          # 7) Heterogeneity → IVW FE vs RE
          #----------------------------------------------------
          het0 <- TwoSampleMR::mr_heterogeneity(harm)
          q_p <- het0$Q_pval[het0$method == "Inverse variance weighted"]
          use_re <- isTRUE(!is.na(q_p) && q_p < 0.05)
          ivw_method <- if (use_re) "mr_ivw_mre" else "mr_ivw_fe"

          #----------------------------------------------------
          # 8) MR core estimators
          #----------------------------------------------------
          mr <- TwoSampleMR::mr(
            harm,
            method_list = c(
              ivw_method,
              "mr_egger_regression",
              "mr_weighted_median",
              "mr_weighted_mode",
              "mr_simple_mode"
            )
          )

          mr_dt <- as.data.table(mr)[, .(
            exposure = exp,
            outcome  = out,
            method,
            nsnp,
            b,
            se,
            p = pval
          )]

          #----------------------------------------------------
          # 9) Heterogeneity + pleiotropy
          #----------------------------------------------------
          het <- as.data.table(TwoSampleMR::mr_heterogeneity(harm))
          ple <- as.data.table(TwoSampleMR::mr_pleiotropy_test(harm))

          #----------------------------------------------------
          # 10) Steiger directionality
          #----------------------------------------------------
          if (exp %in% names(sample_sizes) && out %in% names(sample_sizes)) {

            harm$samplesize.exposure <- sample_sizes[exp]
            harm$samplesize.outcome  <- sample_sizes[out]

            harm_st <- TwoSampleMR::steiger_filtering(harm)

            steiger_summary <- data.table(
              exposure = exp,
              outcome  = out,
              nsnp_steiger = nrow(harm_st),
              direction_correct_fraction = mean(harm_st$steiger_dir, na.rm = TRUE)
            )

          } else {

            steiger_summary <- data.table(
              exposure = exp,
              outcome  = out,
              nsnp_steiger = NA_integer_,
              direction_correct_fraction = NA_real_
            )
          }

          #----------------------------------------------------
          # 11) Leave-one-out
          #----------------------------------------------------
          loo <- as.data.table(TwoSampleMR::mr_leaveoneout(harm))
          loo_dt <- loo[, .(exposure = exp, outcome = out, SNP, b, se, p)]

          #----------------------------------------------------
          # 12) MR-PRESSO
          #----------------------------------------------------
          presso_summary <- data.table(
            exposure = exp,
            outcome  = out,
            presso_ran = FALSE,
            presso_global_p = NA_real_,
            presso_n_outliers = NA_integer_,
            presso_distortion_p = NA_real_
          )

          if (run_presso &&
              requireNamespace("MRPRESSO", quietly = TRUE) &&
              n_final >= 4) {

            presso_in <- data.frame(
              BetaOutcome  = harm$beta.outcome,
              BetaExposure = harm$beta.exposure,
              SdOutcome    = harm$se.outcome,
              SdExposure   = harm$se.exposure,
              SNP          = harm$SNP
            )

            presso_out <- tryCatch(
              MRPRESSO::mr_presso(
                BetaOutcome = "BetaOutcome",
                BetaExposure = "BetaExposure",
                SdOutcome = "SdOutcome",
                SdExposure = "SdExposure",
                OUTLIERtest = TRUE,
                DISTORTIONtest = TRUE,
                data = presso_in,
                NbDistribution = presso_nb,
                SignifThreshold = presso_sig
              ),
              error = function(e) NULL
            )

            if (!is.null(presso_out)) {

              global_p <- as.numeric(presso_out$`MR-PRESSO results`$`Global Test`$Pvalue)
              distortion_p <- as.numeric(presso_out$`MR-PRESSO results`$`Distortion Test`$Pvalue)

              out_tbl <- presso_out$`MR-PRESSO results`$`Outlier Test`
              n_out <- ifelse(is.data.frame(out_tbl), nrow(out_tbl), 0)

              presso_summary <- data.table(
                exposure = exp,
                outcome  = out,
                presso_ran = TRUE,
                presso_global_p = global_p,
                presso_n_outliers = n_out,
                presso_distortion_p = distortion_p
              )
            }
          }

          #====================================================
          # STORE RESULTS
          #====================================================
          mr_results[[k]] <- mr_dt
          mr_het[[k]]     <- het[, .(exposure, outcome, method, Q, Q_df, Q_pval)]
          mr_pleio[[k]]   <- ple[, .(exposure, outcome, egger_intercept, se, pval)]
          mr_steiger[[k]] <- steiger_summary
          mr_loo[[k]]     <- loo_dt
          mr_presso[[k]]  <- presso_summary

          #====================================================
          # FINAL QC ROW (ALWAYS LOGGED)
          #====================================================
          mr_qc[[k]] <- data.table(
            exposure = exp,
            outcome  = out,
            snps_full_matrix = n_full,
            snps_gws = n_gws,
            snps_after_confounder = n_after_confounder,
            snps_after_clumping = n_after_clump,
            snps_after_harmonisation = n_after_harmonise,
            snps_after_fstat = n_after_fstat,
            snps_final = n_final
          )

          k <- k + 1
          
          # 🔥 CLEAN HERE
          rm(harm, exp_dat, out_dat, het, ple, loo_dt, steiger_summary, mr_dt, presso_summary)
          gc(FALSE)

        }
      }
  #----------------------------------------------------
  # Manual cleanup (per exposure)
  #----------------------------------------------------
  rm(exp_df, inst, inst0)
  gc(FALSE)

  cat("✅ Done exposure:", exp, "\n")
}



#============================================================
# COMPLETE SNP ATTRITION TABLE (CREATE ONCE — NO DUPLICATES)
#============================================================
library(data.table)

mr_flow <- rbindlist(mr_qc)

# (optional but very safe)
setkey(mr_flow, exposure, outcome)
mr_flow <- unique(mr_flow)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Combine MR outputs (lists → data.tables)
#------------------------------------------------------------

mr_results <- rbindlist(mr_results, fill = TRUE)
mr_het     <- rbindlist(mr_het,     fill = TRUE)
mr_pleio   <- rbindlist(mr_pleio,   fill = TRUE)
mr_steiger <- rbindlist(mr_steiger, fill = TRUE)
mr_loo     <- rbindlist(mr_loo,     fill = TRUE)
mr_presso  <- rbindlist(mr_presso,  fill = TRUE)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Deduplicate main MR results just in case
#------------------------------------------------------------

mr_results <- mr_results[!duplicated(mr_results[, .(exposure, outcome, method)])]

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Sort main MR results
#------------------------------------------------------------

setorder(mr_results, outcome, p)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Print main results + key diagnostics
#------------------------------------------------------------

print(mr_results)

cat("\n--- Heterogeneity (Q) ---\n")
print(mr_het)

cat("\n--- Egger intercept (pleiotropy) ---\n")
print(mr_pleio)

cat("\n--- Steiger directionality summary ---\n")
print(mr_steiger)

cat("\n--- MR-PRESSO summary ---\n")
print(mr_presso)

cat("\n--- QC (instrument attrition) ---\n")
print(mr_flow)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Save paper-style outputs
#------------------------------------------------------------

saveRDS(mr_results, "mr_results_paperstyle.rds")
saveRDS(mr_het,     "mr_heterogeneity_paperstyle.rds")
saveRDS(mr_pleio,   "mr_pleiotropy_paperstyle.rds")
saveRDS(mr_steiger, "mr_steiger_paperstyle.rds")
saveRDS(mr_loo,     "mr_leaveoneout_paperstyle.rds")
saveRDS(mr_presso,  "mr_presso_paperstyle.rds")
saveRDS(mr_flow,    "mr_flow_paperstyle.rds")
```

# 14. Reloading of Paper-Style MR Results and Diagnostics Objects

All causal estimates, heterogeneity metrics, pleiotropy tests, sensitivity analyses, and instrument-flow QC logs are restored from disk to enable reproducible downstream visualization, reporting, and interpretation.

## 14.1 Restoring causal estimates, sensitivity outputs, and QC logs from disk

Previously saved MR result objects are reloaded into the working environment, ensuring consistent access to causal effect estimates and diagnostic outputs without rerunning computationally intensive analyses.

```{r MRpaperFigures00, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=6, fig.height=5, dpi=300, include=TRUE}


############################################################
# SECTION 14 — Reloading paper-style MR results & diagnostics
# (robust, reproducible, class-safe for all downstream steps)
############################################################

#------------------------------------------------------------
# 14.1 Restore all saved MR objects from disk
#------------------------------------------------------------

files <- list(
  mr_results  = "mr_results_paperstyle.rds",
  mr_het      = "mr_heterogeneity_paperstyle.rds",
  mr_pleio    = "mr_pleiotropy_paperstyle.rds",
  mr_steiger  = "mr_steiger_paperstyle.rds",
  mr_loo      = "mr_leaveoneout_paperstyle.rds",
  mr_presso   = "mr_presso_paperstyle.rds",
  mr_flow     = "mr_flow_paperstyle.rds"
)

message("📂 Reloading MR result objects...")

mr_objects <- lapply(files, function(f) {
  if (!file.exists(f)) stop("Missing file: ", f)
  readRDS(f)
})

list2env(mr_objects, envir = .GlobalEnv)

message("✅ All MR objects restored")

#------------------------------------------------------------
# 14.2 Normalize object classes (CRITICAL for dplyr pipeline)
#------------------------------------------------------------

normalize_df <- function(x) {
  if (inherits(x, "data.table")) return(as.data.frame(x))
  if (is.matrix(x)) return(as.data.frame(x))
  x
}

mr_results <- normalize_df(mr_results)
mr_het     <- normalize_df(mr_het)
mr_pleio   <- normalize_df(mr_pleio)
mr_steiger <- normalize_df(mr_steiger)
mr_loo     <- normalize_df(mr_loo)
mr_presso  <- normalize_df(mr_presso)
mr_flow    <- normalize_df(mr_flow)

message("🧹 Objects converted to data.frame for tidy workflows")

#------------------------------------------------------------
# 14.3 Integrity checks (fast, catches silent corruption)
#------------------------------------------------------------

check_nonempty <- function(obj, name) {
  if (!is.data.frame(obj) || nrow(obj) == 0)
    stop("❌ ", name, " is empty or not a data.frame")
}

check_nonempty(mr_results, "mr_results")
check_nonempty(mr_het,     "mr_het")
check_nonempty(mr_pleio,   "mr_pleio")
check_nonempty(mr_steiger,"mr_steiger")
check_nonempty(mr_loo,     "mr_loo")
check_nonempty(mr_presso,  "mr_presso")
check_nonempty(mr_flow,    "mr_flow")

message("🧪 Integrity checks passed")

#------------------------------------------------------------
# 14.4 Quick summary (for Rmd log)
#------------------------------------------------------------

cat("\nReload summary:\n")
cat("  mr_results rows :", nrow(mr_results), "\n")
cat("  mr_het rows     :", nrow(mr_het), "\n")
cat("  mr_pleio rows   :", nrow(mr_pleio), "\n")
cat("  mr_steiger rows:", nrow(mr_steiger), "\n")
cat("  mr_loo rows     :", nrow(mr_loo), "\n")
cat("  mr_presso rows :", nrow(mr_presso), "\n")
cat("  mr_flow rows   :", nrow(mr_flow), "\n")

message("\n🚀 MR pipeline ready for Sections 15.x")


```



# 15. Main Mendelian Randomization Visualizations

This section presents the primary causal effect estimates and full sensitivity diagnostics from the Mendelian Randomization analyses, including forest plots, comprehensive result tables, heterogeneity assessments, pleiotropy tests, instrument strength summaries, and SNP-level robustness visualizations.

## 15.0 Study variables and instrument filtering overview for GWAS, Elastic Net, and Mendelian Randomization analyses

This section summarizes all phenotypes incorporated across the analytical framework, including accelerometry-derived physical activity traits, biological system predictors, and aging-related outcomes. For each variable, key metadata are reported, including biological domain, analytical role (exposure or outcome), and data source, ensuring transparent and reproducible trait selection.

In addition, a comprehensive SNP attrition table is provided to document the sequential filtering of genetic instruments for Mendelian Randomization analyses, including genome-wide significance selection, LD clumping, confounder screening using PhenoScanner-equivalent PheWAS resources, allele harmonization, and weak-instrument removal. This flow summary enables full traceability of instrument construction across all exposure–outcome pairs and aligns with current best-practice reporting standards for MR studies.

```{r MRpaperFigures0, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=TRUE}
#============================================================

wb <- createWorkbook()

addWorksheet(wb, sheet_name)

title_style <- createStyle(fontSize = 14, textDecoration = "bold")

strong_style <- createStyle(fgFill = "#E8F8F5")

  startRow = 2,
  startCol = 1
)

addStyle(wb, sheet_name, title_style, rows = 1, cols = 1, gridExpand = TRUE)

  wb,
  sheet_name,
  mr_flow_display,
  startRow = 3,
  withFilter = TRUE
)

addStyle(
  wb,
  sheet_name,
  header_style,
  rows = 3,
  cols = 1:ncol(mr_flow_display),
  gridExpand = TRUE
)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(mr_flow_display))) {

  excel_row <- i + 3

  if (mr_flow_display$snps_final[i] == 0) {
    addStyle(
      wb, sheet_name, fail_style,
      rows = excel_row,
      cols = 1:ncol(mr_flow_display),
      gridExpand = TRUE, stack = TRUE
    )
  }

  if (mr_flow_display$snps_final[i] >= 10) {
    addStyle(
      wb, sheet_name, strong_style,
      rows = excel_row,
      cols = 1:ncol(mr_flow_display),
      gridExpand = TRUE, stack = TRUE
    )
  }
}

)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: build flow diagram from real MR row
#------------------------------------------------------------

make_flow_from_row <- function(row) {

  grViz(sprintf("
  digraph MRflow {
    graph [layout = dot, rankdir = TB]

    node [shape = box, style = filled, fillcolor = \"#F8F9F9\", fontname = Helvetica]

    A [label = \"All harmonised SNPs\\n(n = %s)\"]
    B [label = \"Genome-wide significant SNPs\\n(n = %s)\"]
    C [label = \"After LD clumping\\n(n = %s)\"]
    D [label = \"After confounder screening\\n(n = %s)\"]
    E [label = \"After harmonisation\\n(n = %s)\"]
    F [label = \"After weak-instrument filtering (F ≥ 10)\\n(n = %s)\"]
    G [label = \"Final MR instruments\\n(n = %s)\", fillcolor = \"#E8F8F5\"]

    A -> B -> C -> D -> E -> F -> G
  }
  ",
  row$snps_full_matrix,
  row$snps_gws,
  row$snps_after_clumping,
  row$snps_after_confounder,
  row$snps_after_harmonisation,
  row$snps_after_fstat,
  row$snps_final
  ))
}

#------------------------------------------------------------

#------------------------------------------------------------

for (trait in representative_traits) {

  row <- mr_flow %>%
    filter(exposure == trait, outcome == outcome_pick) %>%
    slice(1)

  if (nrow(row) == 0) next

  cat("\n\n### ", trait, " — SNP filtering workflow\n\n")

}
```

## 15.1 Inverse-variance weighted (IVW) forest plots across outcomes

Forest plots display the main IVW causal effect estimates and 95% confidence intervals for all exposure–outcome pairs, stratified by aging outcomes, providing a concise overview of the magnitude and direction of inferred causal relationships.

```{r MRpaperFigures1, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=6, fig.height=5, dpi=300, include=TRUE}


library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Prepare IVW results
#------------------------------------------------------------

ivw <- mr_results %>%
  filter(method == "Inverse variance weighted (multiplicative random effects)") %>%
  mutate(
    ci_low  = b - 1.96 * se,
    ci_high = b + 1.96 * se,
    sig = ifelse(p < 0.05, "p < 0.05", "NS")
  )

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Nature-style forest plot
#------------------------------------------------------------

ggplot(ivw, aes(x = b, y = reorder(exposure, abs(b)))) +

  # subtle null band
  annotate(
    "rect",
    xmin = -0.02, xmax = 0.02,
    ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
    fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.3
  ) +

  # confidence intervals
  geom_errorbarh(
    aes(xmin = ci_low, xmax = ci_high),
    height = 0.28,
    linewidth = 0.9,
    color = "grey30"
  ) +

  # effect points (size = number of SNP instruments)
  geom_point(
    aes(color = sig, size = nsnp),
    alpha = 0.9
  ) +

  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +

  facet_wrap(~ outcome, scales = "free_x") +

  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("p < 0.05" = "#1B9E77", "NS" = "grey50")
  ) +

  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 5)) +

  labs(
    x = "Causal effect (IVW β ± 95% CI)",
    y = "",
    title = "Two-sample Mendelian randomization (IVW)",
    subtitle = "Point size reflects number of instruments; color denotes p-value"
  ) +

  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +

  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_blank()
  )



```
