```{r MRpaperFigures2, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=6, fig.height=5, dpi=300, include=TRUE}
#============================================================
# SECTION 15.2.1 — Table 1. Significant MR results (IVW RE)
# Adds: FDR q-values + robustness flag + ranking + image export
#============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(gt)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Metadata + output
#------------------------------------------------------------
section_id <- "15.2.1"
out_dir <- "C:/Users/75118/Desktop/UEA/Proyecto 1/MainMRresults"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

img_file <- file.path(out_dir, paste0("Section_", section_id, "_Table_1_Significant_MR_IVW_RE.png"))

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: format p-values nicely
#------------------------------------------------------------
fmt_p <- function(x) {
  ifelse(x < 1e-3, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", x))
}

#------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Pull the primary method: IVW random effects
#    (in your object it is "Inverse variance weighted (multiplicative random effects)")
#------------------------------------------------------------
ivw_re <- mr_results %>%
  filter(method == "Inverse variance weighted (multiplicative random effects)") %>%
  mutate(
    ci_low  = b - 1.96 * se,
    ci_high = b + 1.96 * se
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(exposure, outcome, nsnp, b, se, ci_low, ci_high, p)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Get support from other methods (robustness)
#    Weighted median + MR Egger (if present)
#------------------------------------------------------------
wm <- mr_results %>%
  filter(method == "Weighted median") %>%
  dplyr::select(exposure, outcome, b_wm = b, p_wm = p)

egger <- mr_results %>%
  filter(method == "MR Egger") %>%
  dplyr::select(exposure, outcome, b_egger = b, p_egger = p)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Build summary table with:
#    - FDR q (computed across IVW tests)
#    - robustness flag
#------------------------------------------------------------
tab1 <- ivw_re %>%
  left_join(wm, by = c("exposure", "outcome")) %>%
  left_join(egger, by = c("exposure", "outcome")) %>%
  mutate(
    q = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"),

    # Support flags
    wm_support = !is.na(p_wm) & (p_wm < 0.05) & (sign(b_wm) == sign(b)),
    egger_support = !is.na(p_egger) & (p_egger < 0.05) & (sign(b_egger) == sign(b)),

    robustness = case_when(
      wm_support ~ "Robust (WM support)",
      egger_support ~ "Supported (Egger)",
      TRUE ~ "IVW-only"
    ),

    effect_ci = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", b, ci_low, ci_high),
    p_label   = fmt_p(p),
    q_label   = fmt_p(q)
  ) %>%
  # keep significant (choose one: nominal p or FDR)
  filter(p < 0.05) %>%
  group_by(outcome) %>%
  mutate(rank_within_outcome = rank(-abs(b), ties.method = "first")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(outcome, rank_within_outcome) %>%
  transmute(
    Exposure = exposure,
    Outcome  = outcome,
    Instruments = nsnp,
    `β (95% CI)` = effect_ci,
    `P-value` = p_label,
    `FDR q`   = q_label,
    `Robustness` = robustness
  )

#------------------------------------------------------------
# 4) Show in R Markdown (scrollable + searchable alternative)
#    Option A: kableExtra (scroll)
#------------------------------------------------------------
kbl(
  tab1,
  caption = paste0("Table 1. Significant Mendelian Randomization results (IVW random-effects) — Section ", section_id),
  align = "c"
) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, position = "center",
                bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover")) %>%
  scroll_box(height = "500px", width = "100%")

#------------------------------------------------------------
# 5) Export a publication-ready PNG using gt
#------------------------------------------------------------
gt_tbl <- gt(tab1) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = md("**Table 1. Significant Mendelian Randomization results**"),
    subtitle = md(paste0("IVW random-effects estimates (Section ", section_id, "); FDR shown across IVW tests"))
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    `β (95% CI)` = md("&beta; (95% CI)")
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = list(cell_text(weight = "bold")),
    locations = cells_body(columns = c(Exposure, Outcome))
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_body(columns = `P-value`, rows = `P-value` %in% c("<0.001"))
  ) %>%
  opt_all_caps(FALSE) %>%
  opt_table_outline() %>%
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = md("Robustness flag: WM support = Weighted median p < 0.05 with same direction as IVW. FDR q-values computed across IVW tests.")
  )


if(interactive()){
  gtsave(
    gt_tbl,
    filename = img_file,
    vwidth = 2200,
    vheight = 1600,
    expand = 10,
    delay = 2
  )
}


cat("🖼️ Saved Table 1 image at:\n", img_file, "\n")




```




## 15.3 Robustness diagnostics across heterogeneity, pleiotropy, Steiger filtering, and MR-PRESSO

Sensitivity metrics are integrated across methods to flag potential violations of MR assumptions, including instrument heterogeneity, horizontal pleiotropy, directionality inconsistencies, and outlier-driven distortions.

```{r MRpaperFigures3, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=TRUE}


# TABLE 2 — Sensitivity summary


sensitivity <- mr_results %>%
  dplyr::filter(method == "Inverse variance weighted (multiplicative random effects)") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    mr_het %>% dplyr::select(exposure, outcome, Q_pval),
    by = c("exposure","outcome")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    mr_pleio %>% dplyr::select(exposure, outcome, egger_p = pval),
    by = c("exposure","outcome")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    mr_steiger,
    by = c("exposure","outcome")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    mr_presso %>% 
      dplyr::select(exposure, outcome, global_p = presso_global_p),
    by = c("exposure","outcome")
  )


library(kableExtra)
library(dplyr)

sensitivity2 <- sensitivity %>%
  mutate(
    heterogeneity_flag = ifelse(Q_pval < 0.05, "⚠️ Yes", "No"),
    pleiotropy_flag    = ifelse(egger_p < 0.05, "⚠️ Yes", "No"),
    presso_flag        = ifelse(global_p < 0.05, "⚠️ Yes", "No")
  ) %>%
  arrange(outcome, p)


DT::datatable(

#============================================================
# SECTION 15.3.1 — Sensitivity diagnostics (DT full, FDR)
# SECTION 15.3.2 — Simplified sensitivity summary (robust + top N)
#============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(DT)
library(htmltools)
library(gt)

out_dir <- "C:/Users/75118/Desktop/UEA/Proyecto 1/MainMRresults"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Join IVW RE effect sizes into sensitivity (so we can rank)
#------------------------------------------------------------
ivw_re_eff <- mr_results %>%
  filter(method == "Inverse variance weighted (multiplicative random effects)") %>%
  transmute(
    exposure, outcome,
    b_ivw = b,
    se_ivw = se,
    p_ivw = p,
    ci_low = b - 1.96 * se,
    ci_high = b + 1.96 * se
  )

sens_base <- sensitivity %>%
  left_join(ivw_re_eff, by = c("exposure", "outcome")) %>%
  mutate(
    # FDR across IVW tests (use p_ivw if available; fallback to p)
    p_for_fdr = ifelse(!is.na(p_ivw), p_ivw, p),
    q = p.adjust(p_for_fdr, method = "BH"),

    Heterogeneity = ifelse(Q_pval < 0.05, "⚠️ Yes", "No"),
    Pleiotropy    = ifelse(egger_p < 0.05, "⚠️ Yes", "No"),
    Outliers      = ifelse(global_p < 0.05, "⚠️ Yes", "No"),

    Direction_OK = ifelse(direction_correct_fraction >= 0.5, "Yes", "No"),
    Direction_fraction = round(direction_correct_fraction, 2),

    reliability_score =
      (Q_pval >= 0.05) +
      (egger_p >= 0.05) +
      (global_p >= 0.05) +
      (direction_correct_fraction >= 0.5),

    Reliability = case_when(
      reliability_score == 4 ~ "Very strong",
      reliability_score == 3 ~ "Strong",
      reliability_score == 2 ~ "Moderate",
      TRUE ~ "Weak"
    ),

    effect_ci = ifelse(
      !is.na(b_ivw),
      sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", b_ivw, ci_low, ci_high),
      NA_character_
    )
  )

#============================================================
# SECTION 15.3.1 — FULL TABLE (still large, but searchable)
#============================================================

sens_tab_full <- sens_base %>%
  dplyr::filter(q < 0.05) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(outcome, desc(reliability_score), q) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    exposure, outcome,
    effect_ci,
    p_for_fdr, q,
    Heterogeneity, Pleiotropy, Outliers,
    Direction_OK, Direction_fraction,
    Reliability
  ) %>%
  dplyr::rename(p = p_for_fdr)


DT::datatable(
  sens_tab_full,
  rownames = FALSE,
  filter = "top",
  options = list(pageLength = 20, scrollX = TRUE, autoWidth = TRUE),
  caption = tags$caption(
    style = "caption-side: top; text-align: center; font-weight: bold;",
    "Table 2. Sensitivity and robustness diagnostics for IVW MR results (FDR q < 0.05) — Section 15.3.1"
  )
)

#=================================================

#============================================================
# SECTION 15.3.2 — Simplified sensitivity summary (UPGRADED)
# - Less harsh robustness scoring (weighted)
# - Color-coded warning flags in PNG table
# - Star system for strongest causal evidence
# - One-page causal evidence figure (Nature-style)
#============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(DT)
library(htmltools)
library(gt)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)


#------------------------------------------------------------
# Metadata + output
#------------------------------------------------------------
section_id <- "15.3.2"
out_dir <- "C:/Users/75118/Desktop/UEA/Proyecto 1/MainMRresults"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

png_table_file <- file.path(out_dir, paste0("Section_", section_id, "_Table_2a_Simplified_Sensitivity_Summary.png"))
pdf_fig_file   <- file.path(out_dir, paste0("Section_", section_id, "_Figure_Causal_Evidence_OnePage.pdf"))
png_fig_file   <- file.path(out_dir, paste0("Section_", section_id, "_Figure_Causal_Evidence_OnePage.png"))

top_n_per_outcome <- 20  # adjust: 10–25 is usually best for a "simplified" table

#------------------------------------------------------------
# REQUIREMENT: sens_base should exist from Section 15.3.1 build
# sens_base should contain at least:
# exposure, outcome, nsnp, b_ivw, se_ivw, p_for_fdr, q,
# Q_pval, egger_p, global_p, direction_correct_fraction
#------------------------------------------------------------
if (!exists("sens_base")) {
  stop("Object 'sens_base' not found. Please run Section 15.3.1 code that builds 'sens_base' first.")
}

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
#------------------------------------------------------------
fmt_p <- function(x) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(x) ~ NA_character_,
    x < 1e-100 ~ "<1e-100",
    x < 1e-10  ~ format(x, scientific = TRUE, digits = 2),
    x < 1e-3   ~ "<0.001",
    TRUE       ~ sprintf("%.3f", x)
  )
}

safe_ok <- function(x, cutoff = 0.05) {
  # treat NA as "unknown" rather than failure
  ifelse(is.na(x), NA, x >= cutoff)
}

safe_flag <- function(x, cutoff = 0.05) {
  # TRUE means warning flag
  ifelse(is.na(x), NA, x < cutoff)
}

#------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Build upgraded simplified table base
#    - Less harsh score: Steiger + Pleiotropy/Outliers weighted,
#      heterogeneity is down-weighted (very common in polygenic MR)
#------------------------------------------------------------
sens2 <- sens_base %>%
  mutate(
    ci_low  = b_ivw - 1.96 * se_ivw,
    ci_high = b_ivw + 1.96 * se_ivw,
    effect_ci = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", b_ivw, ci_low, ci_high),

    # Flags (TRUE = warning)
    flag_het   = safe_flag(Q_pval, 0.05),
    flag_pleio = safe_flag(egger_p, 0.05),
    flag_out   = safe_flag(global_p, 0.05),

    # Steiger directionality (use 0.5 threshold)
    steiger_ok = ifelse(is.na(direction_correct_fraction), NA, direction_correct_fraction >= 0.50),
    steiger_frac = round(direction_correct_fraction, 2),

    # Display-friendly labels
    Heterogeneity = dplyr::case_when(
      is.na(flag_het)   ~ "NA",
      flag_het          ~ "\u26A0 Yes",
      TRUE              ~ "No"
    ),
    Pleiotropy = dplyr::case_when(
      is.na(flag_pleio) ~ "NA",
      flag_pleio        ~ "\u26A0 Yes",
      TRUE              ~ "No"
    ),
    Outliers = dplyr::case_when(
      is.na(flag_out)   ~ "NA",
      flag_out          ~ "\u26A0 Yes",
      TRUE              ~ "No"
    ),
    Direction_OK = dplyr::case_when(
      is.na(steiger_ok) ~ "NA",
      steiger_ok        ~ "Yes",
      TRUE              ~ "No"
    ),

    #--------------------------------------------------------
    # Less harsh robustness scoring (weighted)
    #  - Steiger is most important (weight 2)
    #  - Pleiotropy and outliers are important (weight 1 each)
    #  - Heterogeneity is common: weight 0.5
    #
    # Score ranges roughly 0–4.5; NA treated as "unknown" (0)
    #--------------------------------------------------------
    score =
      2*(steiger_ok %in% TRUE) +
      1*(flag_out %in% FALSE | is.na(flag_out)) +
      0.5*(flag_pleio %in% FALSE),



    Robustness = case_when(
      score >= 4 ~ "Very strong",
      score >= 3 ~ "Strong",
      score >= 2 ~ "Moderate",
      TRUE       ~ "Weak"
    ),


    #--------------------------------------------------------
    # Star system (strongest causal evidence)
    #  ★★★ : FDR + Steiger OK + no pleiotropy + no outliers
    #   ★★ : FDR + Steiger OK + (<=1 warning among pleio/outliers/het)
    #    ★ : FDR only
    #--------------------------------------------------------
    n_warnings = rowSums(cbind(
      flag_het   %in% TRUE,
      flag_pleio %in% TRUE,
      flag_out   %in% TRUE
    ), na.rm = TRUE),

    Stars = case_when(
      q < 0.05 & isTRUE(steiger_ok) & isFALSE(flag_pleio) & (isFALSE(flag_out) | is.na(flag_out)) ~ "\u2605\u2605\u2605",
      q < 0.05 & isTRUE(steiger_ok) & n_warnings <= 1                                          ~ "\u2605\u2605",
      q < 0.05                                                                                  ~ "\u2605",
      TRUE                                                                                      ~ ""
    ),

    p_label = fmt_p(p_for_fdr),
    q_label = fmt_p(q)
  )

#------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Build simplified table (FDR significant + top N per outcome)
#    Rank: Stars first, then Robustness, then |beta|
#------------------------------------------------------------
robust_order <- c("Very strong", "Strong", "Moderate", "Weak")

#------------------------------------------------------------
# CLEAN + RANK EXACTLY LIKE ORIGINAL (but upgraded metrics)
#------------------------------------------------------------

star_rank <- function(x){
  case_when(
    x == "★★★" ~ 3,
    x == "★★"  ~ 2,
    x == "★"   ~ 1,
    TRUE       ~ 0
  )
}

sens_tab_simple <- sens2 %>%

  # 🔧 critical fix — keep only one row per causal pair
  distinct(exposure, outcome, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%

  # only FDR significant (same as before)
  filter(!is.na(q) & q < 0.05) %>%

  mutate(
    Robustness = factor(Robustness, levels = robust_order),
    star_score = star_rank(Stars),
    abs_b = abs(b_ivw)
  ) %>%

  group_by(outcome) %>%

  arrange(
    desc(star_score),     # strongest stars first (numeric now)
    Robustness,           # Very strong → Weak
    desc(abs_b),
    q,
    .by_group = TRUE
  ) %>%

  slice_head(n = top_n_per_outcome) %>%
  ungroup() %>%

  transmute(
    Exposure = exposure,
    Outcome  = outcome,
    Instruments = nsnp,
    `β (95% CI)` = effect_ci,
    `P` = p_label,
    `FDR q` = q_label,
    Heterogeneity,
    Pleiotropy,
    Outliers,
    `Steiger dir` = Direction_OK,
    `Steiger frac` = steiger_frac,
    Robustness,
    Stars
  )


#------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) R Markdown output: ONE interactive searchable table (DT)
#------------------------------------------------------------
DT::datatable(
  sens_tab_simple,
  rownames = FALSE,
  filter = "top",
  extensions = c("Buttons"),
  options = list(
    dom = "Bfrtip",
    buttons = c("copy", "csv", "excel"),
    pageLength = 15,
    scrollX = TRUE,
    autoWidth = TRUE
  ),
  caption = tags$caption(
    style = "caption-side: top; text-align: center; font-weight: bold;",
    paste0(
      "Table 2a. Simplified sensitivity summary (FDR q < 0.05; top ",
      top_n_per_outcome, " per outcome) — Section ", section_id,
      " | Stars denote strongest causal evidence"
    )
  )
)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# 4) Export publication-ready PNG table (color-coded flags)
#------------------------------------------------------------
gt_tbl <- gt(sens_tab_simple) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = md("**Table 2a. Simplified sensitivity summary**"),
    subtitle = md(paste0(
      "Top ", top_n_per_outcome,
      " most robust associations per outcome (Section ", section_id, "); FDR q < 0.05"
    ))
  ) %>%
  cols_label(`β (95% CI)` = md("&beta; (95% CI)")) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_body(columns = c(Exposure, Outcome, Stars))
  ) %>%
  # Color-code warning flags (Yes) and OK (No)
  tab_style(
    style = cell_fill(color = "#FDEDEC"),  # light red for warnings
    locations = cells_body(columns = c(Heterogeneity, Pleiotropy, Outliers), rows = str_detect(Heterogeneity, "Yes") | str_detect(Pleiotropy, "Yes") | str_detect(Outliers, "Yes"))
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_fill(color = "#EAF2F8"),  # light blue for "No"
    locations = list(
      cells_body(columns = Heterogeneity, rows = Heterogeneity == "No"),
      cells_body(columns = Pleiotropy,    rows = Pleiotropy == "No"),
      cells_body(columns = Outliers,      rows = Outliers == "No")
    )
  ) %>%
  # Highlight robustness level
  tab_style(
    style = cell_fill(color = "#E8F8F5"),  # green-ish
    locations = cells_body(columns = Robustness, rows = Robustness %in% c("Very strong","Strong"))
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_fill(color = "#FEF9E7"),  # yellow-ish
    locations = cells_body(columns = Robustness, rows = Robustness == "Moderate")
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_fill(color = "#F4F6F7"),  # gray-ish
    locations = cells_body(columns = Robustness, rows = Robustness == "Weak")
  ) %>%
  opt_all_caps(FALSE) %>%
  opt_table_outline() %>%
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = md(
      paste0(
        "**Stars:** ★★★ = FDR + Steiger OK + no pleiotropy + no outliers; ★★ = FDR + Steiger OK + ≤1 warning; ★ = FDR only. ",
        "Heterogeneity is down-weighted (common in polygenic MR)."
      )
    )
  )

gtsave(
```

## 15.4 Leave-one-out sensitivity visualizations

Leave-one-out analyses evaluate the influence of individual SNP instruments on causal estimates, ensuring that results are not driven by single variants and highlighting potential influential outliers.

```{r MRpaperFigures4, echo=TRUE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

############################################################
# SECTION 15.4 — Improved Leave-one-out MR sensitivity plots
# (robust, readable, publication-grade)
############################################################

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

#-----------------------------------------------------------
# Output directory
#-----------------------------------------------------------
out_dir <- "C:/Users/75118/Desktop/UEA/Proyecto 1/MainMRresults/LOO_figures_clean"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

#-----------------------------------------------------------
# Select only important MR pairs
# (robust + FDR significant — avoids useless clutter)
#-----------------------------------------------------------

important_pairs <- sens2 %>%      # from Section 15.3.2
  filter(!is.na(q) & q < 0.05) %>%
  distinct(exposure, outcome)

loo_pairs <- mr_loo %>%
  semi_join(important_pairs, by = c("exposure","outcome")) %>%
  distinct(exposure, outcome) %>%
  arrange(outcome, exposure)

#-----------------------------------------------------------
# Improved LOO plotting function
#-----------------------------------------------------------

plot_loo_clean <- function(exp, out, top_snps = 25) {

  df <- mr_loo %>%
    filter(
      exposure == exp,
      outcome == out,
      SNP != "All"
    )

  if (nrow(df) < 3) return(NULL)

  # Baseline IVW estimate (full instrument set)
  ivw_base <- mr_results %>%
    filter(
      exposure == exp,
      outcome == out,
      method == "Inverse variance weighted (multiplicative random effects)"
    ) %>%
    pull(b)

  if (length(ivw_base) == 0) ivw_base <- mean(df$b, na.rm = TRUE)

  # Rank SNPs by absolute influence
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(influence = abs(b)) %>%
    arrange(desc(influence)) %>%
    slice_head(n = top_snps)

  # Flag extreme influence SNPs (top 10%)
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(
      extreme = influence >= quantile(influence, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE)
    )

  ggplot(df, aes(y = reorder(SNP, b), x = b)) +

    # Baseline IVW effect
    geom_vline(
      xintercept = ivw_base,
      color = "black",
      linewidth = 0.6
    ) +

    # Null line
    geom_vline(
      xintercept = 0,
      linetype = "dashed",
      color = "grey50"
    ) +

    # Confidence intervals
    geom_errorbarh(
      aes(xmin = b - 1.96 * se, xmax = b + 1.96 * se),
      height = 0.25,
      color = "grey40"
    ) +

    # Points
    geom_point(
      aes(color = extreme),
      size = 2.3
    ) +

    scale_color_manual(
      values = c(`TRUE` = "#D1495B", `FALSE` = "#2E86AB"),
      labels = c("FALSE" = "Typical SNP", "TRUE" = "High influence")
    ) +

    labs(
      title = paste("LOO MR:", exp, "→", out),
      subtitle = paste("Top", top_snps, "SNPs ranked by influence on IVW estimate"),
      x = "IVW causal effect (β ± 95% CI)",
      y = NULL,
      color = NULL
    ) +

    theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7.5),
      plot.title  = element_text(face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
}

#-----------------------------------------------------------
# Generate + save figures (grouped by outcome)
#-----------------------------------------------------------

outcomes <- unique(loo_pairs$outcome)

for (out in outcomes) {

  # Open collapsible block in Rmd
  cat("\n<details>\n")
  cat(paste0(
    "<summary><b>", out,
    " — Leave-one-out MR sensitivity (cleaned)</b></summary>\n\n"
  ))

  these_pairs <- loo_pairs %>% 
    filter(outcome == out)

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(these_pairs))) {

    exp <- these_pairs$exposure[i]

    p <- plot_loo_clean(exp, out, top_snps = 25)

    if (is.null(p)) next

    file_name <- paste0(
      out_dir, "/LOO_clean_",
      gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]", "_", exp), "_",
      gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]", "_", out), ".png"
    )

    # Save publication-grade figure
    ggsave(
      filename = file_name,
      plot = p,
      width = 6.5,
      height = 5.5,
      dpi = 300
    )

    # Render inline
    print(p)
  }

  cat("\n</details>\n")
}



############################################################
# SECTION 15.4 — Leave-one-out MR sensitivity (TRUE fixed size)
############################################################

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

out_dir <- "C:/Users/75118/Desktop/UEA/Proyecto 1/MainMRresults/15.4_LOO"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)


#-----------------------------------------------------------
# Standardize exposure/outcome naming (case-safe join)
#-----------------------------------------------------------

sens2 <- sens2 %>%
  mutate(
    exposure = toupper(trimws(as.character(exposure))),
    outcome  = toupper(trimws(as.character(outcome)))
  )

mr_loo <- mr_loo %>%
  mutate(
    exposure = toupper(trimws(as.character(exposure))),
    outcome  = toupper(trimws(as.character(outcome)))
  )


mr_results <- mr_results %>%
  mutate(
    exposure = toupper(trimws(as.character(exposure))),
    outcome  = toupper(trimws(as.character(outcome)))
  )

#-----------------------------------------------------------
# Important MR pairs only
#-----------------------------------------------------------

important_pairs <- sens2 %>%
  filter(!is.na(q) & q < 0.05) %>%
  distinct(exposure, outcome)

loo_pairs <- mr_loo %>%
  semi_join(important_pairs, by = c("exposure","outcome")) %>%
  distinct(exposure, outcome)


#-----------------------------------------------------------
# Compute GLOBAL x-limits PER OUTCOME (critical fix)
#-----------------------------------------------------------

x_limits <- mr_loo %>%
  semi_join(loo_pairs, by = c("exposure","outcome")) %>%
  filter(SNP != "All") %>%
  mutate(
    low  = b - 1.96 * se,
    high = b + 1.96 * se
  ) %>%
  group_by(outcome) %>%
  summarise(
    xmin = min(c(low, 0), na.rm = TRUE),
    xmax = max(c(high, 0), na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(pad = 0.05 * (xmax - xmin),
         xmin = xmin - pad,
         xmax = xmax + pad)

#-----------------------------------------------------------
# Final LOO plot (now uses fixed outcome-scale)
#-----------------------------------------------------------

plot_loo_clean <- function(exp, out, top_snps = 25) {

  df <- mr_loo %>%
    filter(exposure == exp, outcome == out, SNP != "All")

  if (nrow(df) < 3) return(NULL)

  ivw_base <- mr_results %>%
    filter(
      exposure == exp,
      outcome == out,
      method == "Inverse variance weighted (multiplicative random effects)"
    ) %>%
    pull(b)

  if (length(ivw_base) == 0) ivw_base <- mean(df$b)

  df <- df %>%
    mutate(influence = abs(b)) %>%
    arrange(desc(influence)) %>%
    slice_head(n = top_snps) %>%
    mutate(extreme = influence >= quantile(influence, 0.90))

  lims <- x_limits %>% filter(outcome == out)

  ggplot(df, aes(y = reorder(SNP, b), x = b)) +

    geom_vline(xintercept = ivw_base, linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +

    geom_errorbarh(
      aes(xmin = b - 1.96 * se, xmax = b + 1.96 * se),
      height = 0.25,
      color = "grey40"
    ) +

    geom_point(aes(color = extreme), size = 2.3) +

    scale_color_manual(
      values = c(`TRUE` = "#D1495B", `FALSE` = "#2E86AB"),
      labels = c("FALSE" = "Typical SNP", "TRUE" = "High influence")
    ) +

    scale_x_continuous(
      limits = c(lims$xmin, lims$xmax),
      expand = c(0, 0)
    ) +

    labs(
      title = paste("LOO MR:", exp, "→", out),
      subtitle = "Top 25 SNPs ranked by influence on IVW estimate",
      x = "IVW causal effect (β ± 95% CI)",
      y = NULL,
      color = NULL
    ) +

    theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7.5),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
      plot.margin = margin(6,6,6,6),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
}

#-----------------------------------------------------------
# Grid export (fixed canvas forever)
#-----------------------------------------------------------

############################################################
# Smart grid export — no empty space, same panel scaling
############################################################

library(cowplot)   # better for tight grids than patchwork

outcomes <- unique(loo_pairs$outcome)

plots_per_row <- 2   # keep 2 columns (journal standard)
max_plots_page <- 6  # still chunk to avoid overcrowding

chunk_list <- function(x, n) split(x, ceiling(seq_along(x)/n))

for (out in outcomes) {

  these_pairs <- loo_pairs %>% filter(outcome == out)
  if (nrow(these_pairs) == 0) next

  plot_list <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(these_pairs)), function(i) {
    plot_loo_clean(these_pairs$exposure[i], out)
  })

  plot_list <- Filter(Negate(is.null), plot_list)

  blocks <- chunk_list(plot_list, max_plots_page)

  for (b in seq_along(blocks)) {

    block <- blocks[[b]]

    # dynamic rows — no empty space
    n_rows <- ceiling(length(block) / plots_per_row)

    block_plot <- plot_grid(
      plotlist = block,
      ncol = plots_per_row,
      nrow = n_rows,
      align = "hv"
    )

    file_name <- file.path(
      out_dir,
      paste0(
        "LOO_Block_",
        gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]", "_", out),
        "_Part_", b,
        ".png"
      )
    )

    # Height scales with rows, width constant → panel size same
    ggsave(
      filename = file_name,
      plot = block_plot,
      width = 12,
      height = 4 * n_rows,   # each row same height
      dpi = 300
    )

    cat("Saved compressed block:", file_name, "\n")
  }
}

############################################################
# SECTION 15.4.1 — Leave-one-out stability summary (quantitative)
############################################################

library(dplyr)
library(gt)
library(kableExtra)
library(openxlsx)

#-----------------------------------------------------------
# Output
#-----------------------------------------------------------

out_dir <- "C:/Users/75118/Desktop/UEA/Proyecto 1/MainMRresults"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

png_file   <- file.path(out_dir, "Section_15.4_LOO_Stability_Summary.png")
excel_file <- file.path(out_dir, "Section_15.4_LOO_Stability_Summary.xlsx")

#-----------------------------------------------------------
# Baseline IVW effects (full instrument set)
#-----------------------------------------------------------

ivw_base <- mr_results %>%
  dplyr::filter(method == "Inverse variance weighted (multiplicative random effects)") %>%
  dplyr::select(exposure, outcome, ivw_b = b)

#-----------------------------------------------------------
# Build LOO stability metrics
#-----------------------------------------------------------

loo_stats <- mr_loo %>%
  filter(SNP != "All") %>%
  group_by(exposure, outcome) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_loo_b = mean(b, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_loo_b   = sd(b, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_loo_b  = min(b, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_loo_b  = max(b, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(ivw_base, by = c("exposure","outcome")) %>%
  mutate(

    # absolute worst deviation from baseline IVW
    max_shift = pmax(
      abs(max_loo_b - ivw_b),
      abs(min_loo_b - ivw_b)
    ),

    # relative % shift
    pct_shift = 100 * max_shift / abs(ivw_b),

    # direction flip check
    direction_flip = ifelse(
      (min_loo_b < 0 & ivw_b > 0) | (max_loo_b > 0 & ivw_b < 0),
      "⚠️ Yes",
      "No"
    ),

    # automatic instability flag (conservative but journal-safe)
    unstable = case_when(
      direction_flip == "⚠️ Yes" ~ "⚠️ Unstable",
      pct_shift > 20             ~ "⚠️ Large shift",
      sd_loo_b > 0.05 * abs(ivw_b) ~ "⚠️ High variability",
      TRUE ~ "Stable"
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(outcome, desc(pct_shift))

#-----------------------------------------------------------
# Clean display table
#-----------------------------------------------------------

loo_display <- loo_stats %>%
  transmute(
    Exposure = exposure,
    Outcome  = outcome,
    `IVW β` = round(ivw_b, 4),
    `Mean LOO β` = round(mean_loo_b, 4),
    `SD across LOO` = round(sd_loo_b, 4),
    `Max shift` = round(max_shift, 4),
    `% shift` = round(pct_shift, 2),
    `Direction flip?` = direction_flip,
    Stability = unstable
  )

#===========================================================
# 1) R MARKDOWN DISPLAY (scrollable)
#===========================================================

kbl(
  loo_display,
  caption = "Table 15.4a. Quantitative leave-one-out stability summary of MR causal estimates",
  align = "c"
) %>%
  kable_styling(
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "center",
    bootstrap_options = c("striped","hover")
  ) %>%
  scroll_box(height = "450px", width = "100%")

#===========================================================
# 2) EXCEL EXPORT
#===========================================================

write.xlsx(

  excel_file,
  overwrite = TRUE
)

#===========================================================

#===========================================================
```

## 15.5 Instrument strength table (F-statistics per exposure)

F-statistics are summarized across exposures to quantify instrument strength and verify that selected genetic instruments exceed conventional weak-instrument thresholds.

```{r MRpaperFigures5, echo=TRUE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

############################################################
# SECTION 15.5 — Instrument strength (IDENTICAL LOGIC)
############################################################

library(data.table)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(gt)

mapped_dir <- "C:/Users/75118/Desktop/UEA/Proyecto 1/mapped_full_traits"


files <- list.files(
  mapped_dir,
  pattern = "^mapped_full_.*\\.rds$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

p_instrument <- 5e-8

out_dir <- "C:/Users/75118/Desktop/UEA/Proyecto 1/MainMRresults"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

png_file <- file.path(out_dir, "Section_15.5_Table_Instrument_Strength.png")

fstats_list <- list()

#------------------------------------------------------------
# IDENTICAL FILTERING AS YOUR ORIGINAL CODE
#------------------------------------------------------------

for (f in files) {

  exp_name <- sub("mapped_full_|\\.rds", "", basename(f))
  
  cat("Processing:", exp_name, "\n")
  flush.console()
  
  exp_df   <- readRDS(f)

  exp_df$P <- 2 * pnorm(-abs(exp_df$BETA / exp_df$SE))
  exp_df$F_stat <- (exp_df$BETA^2) / (exp_df$SE^2)

  inst <- exp_df[exp_df$P < p_instrument & exp_df$F_stat >= 10, ]

  if (nrow(inst) == 0) next

  fstats_list[[exp_name]] <- data.table(
    trait  = exp_name,
    F_stat = inst$F_stat
  )

  rm(exp_df, inst)
  gc(FALSE)
}

fstats_dt <- rbindlist(fstats_list)

f_stats_inst <- fstats_dt %>%
  group_by(trait) %>%
  summarise(
    n_snps = n(),
    mean_F = mean(F_stat),
    median_F = median(F_stat),
    min_F  = min(F_stat),
    max_F  = max(F_stat),
    pct_F_ge_30 = round(100 * mean(F_stat >= 30), 1),
    weak_risk = ifelse(min_F < 10, "⚠️ Potential weak", "No"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_F))

#============================================================
# R Markdown display
#============================================================

kbl(
  f_stats_inst,
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Table S2. Instrument strength (F-statistics) for MR-selected instruments",
  align = "c"
) %>%
  kable_styling(
    full_width = FALSE,
    bootstrap_options = c("striped","hover")
  ) %>%
  scroll_box(height = "420px", width = "100%")

#============================================================
# PNG EXPORT — SAME AS YOUR CODE
#============================================================

gt_tbl <- gt(f_stats_inst) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = md("**Instrument strength across MR exposures**"),
    subtitle = md("F-statistics for genome-wide significant instruments (Section 15.5)")
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    trait = "Exposure",
    n_snps = "Instruments",
    mean_F = "Mean F",
    median_F = "Median F",
    min_F = "Min F",
    max_F = "Max F",
    pct_F_ge_30 = "% F ≥ 30",

  ) %>%
  fmt_number(

  ) %>%
  tab_style(

  opt_table_outline() %>%
```

```{r MRpaperFigures6, echo=TRUE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# 🧬 3. Nearest gene mapping (cached + batched)
#====================================================

library(biomaRt)

out_dir <- "C:/Users/75118/Desktop/UEA/Proyecto 1/MainMRresults"
gene_cache_file <- file.path(out_dir, "nearest_gene_cache.rds")

if (file.exists(gene_cache_file)) {

  message("⚡ Loading cached nearest gene mapping")
  nearest_gene <- readRDS(gene_cache_file)

} else {

  message("🌐 Querying Ensembl (first run only)")

  ensembl <- useEnsembl(
    biomart = "ENSEMBL_MART_ENSEMBL",
    dataset = "hsapiens_gene_ensembl",
    GRCh = 37
  )

  regions <- unique(
    paste0(inst$CHR, ":", inst$BP - 1e6, ":", inst$BP + 1e6)
  )

  chunks <- split(regions, ceiling(seq_along(regions) / 500))

  gene_map <- rbindlist(
    lapply(chunks, function(reg) {
      getBM(
        attributes = c(
          "chromosome_name",
          "start_position",
          "end_position",
          "external_gene_name"
        ),
        filters = "chromosomal_region",
        values = reg,
        mart = ensembl
      )
    }),
    fill = TRUE
  )

  setnames(
    gene_map,
    c("chromosome_name","start_position","end_position","external_gene_name"),
    c("CHR","start","end","gene")
  )

  pos_map <- inst[, .(CHR, BP)] |> unique()
  
  gene_map[, CHR := as.character(CHR)]
  pos_map[, CHR := as.character(CHR)]

  gene_map <- merge(gene_map, pos_map, by = "CHR", allow.cartesian = TRUE)

  gene_map[, dist := abs(start - BP)]

  nearest_gene <- gene_map[
    , .SD[which.min(dist)],
    by = .(CHR, BP)
  ][, .(CHR, BP, gene)]

  saveRDS(nearest_gene, gene_cache_file)

  message("💾 Nearest gene mapping cached")
}
```

Scatter plots visualize SNP-specific associations between exposures and outcomes, illustrating consistency of instrument effects and the linear relationship underpinning IVW causal estimates.

```{r MRpaperFigures7, echo=TRUE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

###################################################
# SECTION 15.7 — MR scatter plot grids (ROBUST FIX)
###################################################

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

out_dir <- "C:/Users/75118/Desktop/UEA/Proyecto 1/MainMRresults/15.7_ScatterGrids"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

#-------------------------------------------------
# Top robust MR pairs
#-------------------------------------------------

top_pairs <- sens_tab_simple %>%
  group_by(Outcome) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  transmute(
    exposure = Exposure,
    outcome  = Outcome
  )

#-------------------------------------------------
# SNP-level MR data
#-------------------------------------------------

mr_snps <- unique(mr_loo$SNP)

# 🔥 Build minimal SNP-level dataset exposure-by-exposure
mapped_dir <- "C:/Users/75118/Desktop/UEA/Proyecto 1/mapped_full_traits"

files <- list.files(
  mapped_dir,
  pattern = "^mapped_full_.*\\.rds$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

dt_list <- list()

for (f in files) {

  exp_name <- gsub("mapped_full_|\\.rds$", "", basename(f))


  cat("Loading:", exp_name, "\n")
  flush.console()

  exp_df <- readRDS(f)

  # Immediately restrict to SNPs used in MR
  exp_df <- exp_df[exp_df$SNP %in% mr_snps, ]

  if (nrow(exp_df) == 0) {
    rm(exp_df)
    gc(FALSE)
    next
  }

  exp_df$trait <- exp_name

  dt_list[[exp_name]] <- exp_df[, c("trait","SNP","BETA","SE")]

  rm(exp_df)
  gc(FALSE)
}



dt <- bind_rows(dt_list)

#-------------------------------------------------
# IVW slope lookup (robust to naming)
#-------------------------------------------------

ivw_lookup <- mr_results %>%
  filter(grepl("IVW|variance weighted", method, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
  transmute(
    exposure,
    outcome,
    b_ivw = b
  )

min_snps <- 3
n_label  <- 4
use_repel <- requireNamespace("ggrepel", quietly = TRUE)

outcomes <- unique(top_pairs$outcome)

for (out in outcomes) {

  pairs_out <- top_pairs %>% filter(outcome == out)
  plot_list <- list()

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(pairs_out))) {

    exp <- pairs_out$exposure[i]

    df_exp <- dt %>% filter(trait == exp)
    df_out <- dt %>% filter(trait == out)

    scatter_df <- inner_join(
      df_exp, df_out,
      by = "SNP",
      suffix = c("_exp","_out")
    )

    if (nrow(scatter_df) < min_snps) next

    #---------------------------------------------
    # IVW slope (fallback to lm if missing)
    #---------------------------------------------

    b_ivw <- ivw_lookup %>%
      filter(exposure == exp, outcome == out) %>%
      pull(b_ivw)

    if (length(b_ivw) == 0 || is.na(b_ivw)) {
      b_ivw <- coef(lm(BETA_out ~ BETA_exp - 1, scatter_df))[1]
    }

    #---------------------------------------------
    # Influence diagnostics
    #---------------------------------------------

    scatter_df <- scatter_df %>%
      mutate(
        pred = b_ivw * BETA_exp,
        resid = BETA_out - pred,
        stud_resid = abs(resid / SE_out)
      ) %>%
      arrange(desc(stud_resid)) %>%
      mutate(label_me = row_number() <= n_label)

    x_rng <- range(scatter_df$BETA_exp, na.rm = TRUE)
    line_df <- data.frame(x = x_rng, y = b_ivw * x_rng)

    #---------------------------------------------
    # Build plot
    #---------------------------------------------

    p <- ggplot(scatter_df, aes(BETA_exp, BETA_out)) +

      geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +

      geom_point(
        data = scatter_df %>% filter(label_me),
        color = "#D55E00",
        size = 2.8
      ) +

      geom_line(
        data = line_df,
        aes(x, y),
        linewidth = 1
      ) +

      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +

      labs(
        title = paste(exp, "→", out),
        subtitle = paste0("IVW slope = ", sprintf("%.3f", b_ivw)),
        x = "β exposure",
        y = "β outcome"
      ) +
      theme_bw(base_size = 11)

    if (n_label > 0) {

      lab_df <- scatter_df %>% filter(label_me)

      if (use_repel) {
        p <- p + ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
          data = lab_df,
          aes(label = SNP),
          size = 3
        )
      } else {
        p <- p + geom_text(
          data = lab_df,
          aes(label = SNP),
          size = 3,
          vjust = -0.6
        )
      }
    }

    plot_list[[length(plot_list) + 1]] <- p
  }

  #-------------------------------------------------
  # Save grid
  #-------------------------------------------------

  if (length(plot_list) == 0) next

  grid_plot <- wrap_plots(plot_list, ncol = 2) +
    plot_annotation(
      title = paste("MR scatter plots —", out),
      subtitle = "Robust causal associations (IVW slopes)"
    )

  print(grid_plot)

  ggsave(
    file.path(out_dir, paste0("Section_15.7_MR_Scatter_", out, ".png")),
    grid_plot,
    width = 10,
    height = 8,
    dpi = 300
  )
}



```

## 15.10 Mode-based Mendelian Randomization robustness analyses - Weighted mode MR and Simple mode MR forest plots

```{r MRpaperFigures10, echo=TRUE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=6, fig.height=5, dpi=300}

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Extract mode-based MR results
#------------------------------------------------------------

mode_mr <- mr_results %>%
  filter(method %in% c("Weighted mode", "Simple mode")) %>%
  mutate(
    ci_low  = b - 1.96 * se,
    ci_high = b + 1.96 * se
  )

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot function per outcome
#------------------------------------------------------------

plot_mode_forest <- function(out) {

  df <- mode_mr %>% filter(outcome == out)

  if (nrow(df) < 3) return(NULL)

  ggplot(df,
         aes(
           x = b,
           y = reorder(exposure, b),
           color = method
         )) +
    geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), size = 2) +
    geom_errorbarh(
      aes(xmin = ci_low, xmax = ci_high),
      height = 0.2,
      position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)
    ) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    facet_wrap(~ method, scales = "free_x") +
    labs(
      x = "Causal effect (β ± 95% CI)",
      y = "",
      title = paste("Mode-based MR robustness:", out)
    ) +
    theme_bw()
}

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Render plots for all outcomes
#------------------------------------------------------------

outcomes <- unique(mode_mr$outcome)

for (out in outcomes) {
  p <- plot_mode_forest(out)
  if (!is.null(p)) print(p)
}
```

## 15.11 Cross-estimator robustness and concordance across Mendelian Randomization methods

To evaluate consistency of causal inference across complementary MR estimators, effect sizes derived from IVW, weighted median, weighted mode, and simple mode methods were jointly compared. Integrated visualizations assess agreement in magnitude, directionality, and statistical stability across exposure–outcome relationships, providing a comprehensive robustness framework against pleiotropy and instrument invalidity.


```{r MRpaperFigures11, echo=TRUE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=6, fig.height=5, dpi=300}

############################################################
# SECTION 15.11 — Cross-estimator robustness (FIXED)
############################################################

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Prepare combined MR estimates (robust methods only)
#------------------------------------------------------------
robust_mr <- mr_results %>%
  filter(method %in% c(
    "Inverse variance weighted (multiplicative random effects)",
    "Weighted median",
    "Weighted mode",
    "Simple mode"
  )) %>%
  mutate(
    ci_low  = b - 1.96 * se,
    ci_high = b + 1.96 * se,
    method = recode(method,
      "Inverse variance weighted (multiplicative random effects)" = "IVW (Random Effects)",
      "Weighted median" = "Weighted median",
      "Weighted mode"   = "Weighted mode",
      "Simple mode"     = "Simple mode"
    ),
    outcome = recode(outcome,
      "Parental_lifespan"  = "Parental lifespan",
      "Usual_walking_pace" = "Usual walking pace"
    )
  )

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Robust IVW-based ordering per outcome (NO NA POSSIBLE)
#------------------------------------------------------------
robust_mr2 <- robust_mr %>%
  group_by(outcome) %>%
  mutate(
    ivw_effect = b[method == "IVW (Random Effects)"][
      match(exposure,
            exposure[method == "IVW (Random Effects)"])
    ]
  ) %>%
  arrange(outcome, ivw_effect) %>%
  mutate(
    exposure_plot = factor(exposure, levels = unique(exposure))
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Combined cross-estimator forest plot
#------------------------------------------------------------
ggplot(robust_mr2,
       aes(x = b,
           y = exposure_plot,
           color = method)) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(0.6), size = 2) +
  geom_errorbarh(
    aes(xmin = ci_low, xmax = ci_high),
    height = 0.2,
    position = position_dodge(0.6)
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ outcome, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    x = "Causal effect (β ± 95% CI)",
    y = "",
    title = "Cross-estimator Mendelian Randomization robustness"
  ) +
  scale_color_discrete(labels = \(x) str_wrap(x, 35)) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 5.5),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 20, 35, 20)
  ) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(ncol = 1, byrow = TRUE))





#============================================================
# 15.11.2 Concordance heatmap (method correlation)
#============================================================
mr_wide <- dcast(
  as.data.table(robust_mr),
  exposure + outcome ~ method,
  value.var = "b"
)

mr_corr <- mr_wide[, !c("exposure", "outcome")] |> na.omit()
corr_mat <- cor(mr_corr)

corr_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(corr_mat))
names(corr_df) <- c("Method1", "Method2", "Correlation")

ggplot(corr_df, aes(Method1, Method2, fill = Correlation)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(Correlation, 2)), color = "black", size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", midpoint = 0) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "Concordance of MR effect estimates across methods",
    x = "",
    y = ""
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    plot.title  = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
  )




#============================================================
# 15.11.3 Directional stability heatmap (sign agreement)
#============================================================
sign_long <- robust_mr %>%
  mutate(sign_label = ifelse(b > 0, "Positive", "Negative")) %>%
  dplyr::select(exposure, outcome, method, sign_label)


ggplot(sign_long, aes(method, exposure, fill = sign_label)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.25) +
  facet_wrap(~ outcome, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Positive" = "#D73027", "Negative" = "#4575B4")) +
  labs(
    title = "Directional stability of MR estimates across methods",
    x = "",
    y = ""
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
    plot.title  = element_text(size = 14, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 10, r = 10, b = 10, l = 20)
  )

```


## 15.12 Colocalization analysis of shared causal variants between exposures and aging outcomes

Colocalization analyses were conducted to distinguish true shared causal variants from linkage disequilibrium–driven associations by evaluating regional SNP signals for exposures and outcomes using Bayesian posterior probabilities.

```{r MRpaperColocalization, echo=TRUE, results='hide', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=FALSE}

############################################################
# 15.12 COLOCALIZATION OF EXPOSURE–OUTCOME LOCI
############################################################

library(coloc)
library(dplyr)
library(data.table)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(DT)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Sample sizes per trait (USED BY COLOC) — UPDATED
#------------------------------------------------------------

sample_sizes <- c(

  #==========================================================
  # Primary PA
  #==========================================================
  Self_MVPA = 608595,

  #==========================================================
  # Cardiorespiratory / Metabolic Predictors
  #==========================================================
  CRF_slope = 70783,
  CRF_VO2max = 70783,
  Chronotype = 449734,
  CRP = 575531,
  HbA1c = 400825,
  Grip_strength = 404112,
  HDL = 1320016,
  LDL = 1320016,
  Triglycerides = 1320016,
  WBC = 416522,
  VAT = 32860,
  Fat_mass = 412524,
  Fat_free_mass = 413158,
  BMD = 426824,

  #==========================================================
  # Newly Added Traits
  #==========================================================
  Resting_heart_rate = 458969,
  FEV1 = 383471,
  WHR_adjBMI = 694649,
  WC_adjBMI = 365499,
  Smoking_initiation = 1232091,
  Sugar_intake = 454499,

  #==========================================================
  # Device-Based Accelerometry
  #==========================================================
  Acc_total_log = 88411,
  Acc_LIPA = 88411,
  Acc_MVPA = 88411,
  Acc_L5_inactivity = 88411,
  Acc_relative_amplitude = 88411,

  #==========================================================
  # Self-Reported PA / Walking
  #==========================================================
  Leisure_Screen_t = 526725,
  Walking_time = 394642,
  Walking_days = 413244,

  #==========================================================
  # Aging Outcomes
  #==========================================================
  Healthspan = 300447,
  Parental_lifespan = 500193,
  Usual_walking_pace = 417933
)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Significant MR pairs
#------------------------------------------------------------

sig_pairs <- mr_results %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    method == "Inverse variance weighted (multiplicative random effects)",
    p < 0.05
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(exposure, outcome) %>%
  dplyr::distinct()

#------------------------------------------------------------
# SNP → position lookup
#------------------------------------------------------------

pa_ref_file <- files_accel[1]

pa_lookup <- fread(
  pa_ref_file,
  select = c("variant_id","chromosome","base_pair_location"),
  showProgress = FALSE
) %>%
  rename(
    SNP = variant_id,
    chr = chromosome,
    pos = base_pair_location
  ) %>%
  distinct()

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper
#------------------------------------------------------------

to_maf <- function(eaf) pmin(eaf, 1 - eaf)

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Coloc per pair
#------------------------------------------------------------

run_coloc_pair <- function(exp_trait, out_trait, window_bp = 500000) {

  if (is.null(sample_sizes[[exp_trait]]) ||
      is.null(sample_sizes[[out_trait]])) return(NULL)

  # 🔥 Load exposure and outcome separately (no gwas_mr)

  mapped_dir <- "C:/Users/75118/Desktop/UEA/Proyecto 1/mapped_full_traits"

  exp_df <- readRDS(file.path(mapped_dir, paste0("mapped_full_", exp_trait, ".rds")))
  out_df <- readRDS(file.path(mapped_dir, paste0("mapped_full_", out_trait, ".rds")))

  exp_df$trait <- exp_trait
  out_df$trait <- out_trait

  merged <- inner_join(
    exp_df, out_df,
    by = "SNP",
    suffix = c("_exp","_out")
  ) %>%
    inner_join(pa_lookup, by = "SNP") %>%
    filter(!is.na(EAF_exp), !is.na(EAF_out))

  if (nrow(merged) < 200) return(NULL)

  merged <- merged %>%
    mutate(p_exp = 2 * pnorm(-abs(BETA_exp / SE_exp)))

  lead_snps <- merged %>%
    arrange(p_exp) %>%
    slice_head(n = 5) %>%
    pull(SNP)

  out <- list()

  for (lead in lead_snps) {

    center <- merged %>% filter(SNP == lead)
    if (nrow(center) == 0) next

    chr0 <- center$chr[1]
    pos0 <- center$pos[1]

    region <- merged %>%
      filter(chr == chr0, abs(pos - pos0) <= window_bp)

    if (nrow(region) < 100) next

    dataset1 <- list(
      snp     = region$SNP,
      beta    = region$BETA_exp,
      varbeta = region$SE_exp^2,
      MAF     = to_maf(region$EAF_exp),
      N       = sample_sizes[[exp_trait]],
      type    = "quant"
    )

    dataset2 <- list(
      snp     = region$SNP,
      beta    = region$BETA_out,
      varbeta = region$SE_out^2,
      MAF     = to_maf(region$EAF_out),
      N       = sample_sizes[[out_trait]],
      type    = "quant"
    )

    coloc_res <- suppressMessages(
      suppressWarnings(
        tryCatch(
          coloc.abf(dataset1, dataset2),
          error = function(e) NULL
        )
      )
    )

    if (is.null(coloc_res)) next

    out[[lead]] <- data.frame(
      exposure = exp_trait,
      outcome  = out_trait,
      lead_snp = lead,
      chr = chr0,
      center_pos = pos0,
      nsnps_region = nrow(region),
      PP.H0 = coloc_res$summary["PP.H0.abf"],
      PP.H1 = coloc_res$summary["PP.H1.abf"],
      PP.H2 = coloc_res$summary["PP.H2.abf"],
      PP.H3 = coloc_res$summary["PP.H3.abf"],
      PP.H4 = coloc_res$summary["PP.H4.abf"],
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }

  rm(exp_df, out_df, merged)
  gc(FALSE)

  bind_rows(out)
}

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Run across all MR-significant pairs
#------------------------------------------------------------

coloc_results <- bind_rows(
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(sig_pairs)), function(i) {
    run_coloc_pair(
      sig_pairs$exposure[i],
      sig_pairs$outcome[i]
    )
  })
)

coloc_results <- coloc_results %>%
  mutate(PP.H4_percent = round(100 * PP.H4, 2))


#------------------------------------------------------------
# Save results
#------------------------------------------------------------

saveRDS(coloc_results, "coloc_results_paperstyle.rds")


```

```{r MRpaperColocalization2, echo=TRUE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# 1) Map nearby genes (Ensembl biomaRt; GRCh37 friendly)

#============================================================
# COLOC → nearby gene mapping (± window bp)
#============================================================

#============================================================
# FAST nearby gene mapping for all coloc loci (batched)
#============================================================

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tibble)
  library(biomaRt)
})

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Parameters
#------------------------------------------------------------

window_bp <- 500000     # ±500 kb (change if needed)
top_genes <- 8         # number of closest genes to keep per locus

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Collapse coloc to 1 locus per exposure–outcome (highest PP.H4)
#------------------------------------------------------------

coloc_locus <- coloc_clean %>%
  group_by(exposure, outcome, chr) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = PP.H4, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    chr = as.character(chr),
    center_pos = as.integer(center_pos)
  )

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Build genomic windows for all loci
#------------------------------------------------------------

regions <- coloc_locus %>%
  transmute(
    exposure,
    outcome,
    lead_snp,
    chr,
    start = pmax(1L, center_pos - window_bp),
    end   = center_pos + window_bp,
    center_pos,
    PP.H4
  )

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Connect ONCE to Ensembl (GRCh37)
#------------------------------------------------------------

gene_cache_file <- file.path(out_dir, "coloc_gene_annotation_cache.rds")

if (file.exists(gene_cache_file)) {

  message("⚡ Loading cached gene annotation")
  gene_raw <- readRDS(gene_cache_file)

} else {

  message("🌐 Querying Ensembl (first run only)")

  mart <- useEnsembl(
    biomart = "genes",
    dataset = "hsapiens_gene_ensembl",
    GRCh = 37
  )

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Pull ALL genes across ALL regions in one query
#------------------------------------------------------------
  
  gene_raw <- getBM(
    attributes = c(
      "hgnc_symbol",
      "ensembl_gene_id",
      "chromosome_name",
      "start_position",
      "end_position",
      "gene_biotype"
    ),
    filters = c("chromosome_name","start","end"),
    values  = list(regions$chr, regions$start, regions$end),
    mart    = mart
  ) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    filter(hgnc_symbol != "") %>%
    mutate(chromosome_name = as.character(chromosome_name))

  saveRDS(gene_raw, gene_cache_file)
  message("💾 Gene annotation cached")
}


#------------------------------------------------------------
# Match genes back to each locus window + distance to lead SNP
#------------------------------------------------------------

gene_map_fast <- regions %>%
  left_join(
    gene_raw,
    by = c("chr" = "chromosome_name")
  ) %>%
  filter(
    start_position >= start,
    end_position   <= end
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    dist_to_center = pmin(
      abs(start_position - center_pos),
      abs(end_position   - center_pos)
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(exposure, outcome, dist_to_center)


#------------------------------------------------------------
# OPTIONAL — collapse to closest genes per locus (clean table)
#------------------------------------------------------------

gene_annot_fast <- gene_map_fast %>%
  group_by(exposure, outcome, lead_snp, chr, center_pos, PP.H4) %>%
  summarise(
    nearby_genes = paste(
      head(unique(hgnc_symbol), top_genes),
      collapse = ", "
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

#------------------------------------------------------------
# Merge gene annotation back to coloc loci
#------------------------------------------------------------

coloc_locus_annot <- coloc_locus %>%
  left_join(
    gene_annot_fast,
    by = c("exposure","outcome","lead_snp","chr","center_pos","PP.H4")
  )



# 2) Merge coloc tier into your causal robustness score
# A) Build a clean coloc tier + numeric score


#============================================================
# COLOC tier + score
#============================================================

coloc_locus_scored <- coloc_locus_annot %>%
  mutate(
    coloc_strength = case_when(
      PP.H4 >= 0.9 ~ "Very strong",
      PP.H4 >= 0.7 ~ "Strong",
      PP.H4 >= 0.3 ~ "Suggestive",
      TRUE ~ "None"
    ),
    coloc_score = case_when(
      PP.H4 >= 0.9 ~ 3L,
      PP.H4 >= 0.7 ~ 2L,
      PP.H4 >= 0.3 ~ 1L,
      TRUE ~ 0L
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(     # ← this is the fix
    exposure, outcome, PP.H4, coloc_strength, coloc_score,
    lead_snp, chr, center_pos, nearby_genes
  )


datatable(
  coloc_locus_scored,
  extensions = c("Scroller"),
  options = list(
    scrollY = 400,
    scrollX = TRUE,
    scroller = TRUE,
    pageLength = 25
  ),
  rownames = FALSE
)


# B) Merge into your existing “robustness” table

#============================================================
# Merge COLOC into sensitivity robustness table (sens_tab_simple)
#============================================================

robust_with_coloc <- sens_tab_simple %>%
  transmute(
    exposure = Exposure,
    outcome  = Outcome,
    q = `FDR q`,          # ← THIS is the real column
    Robustness,
    Stars,
    b_ivw = NA_real_     # you don’t have b_ivw in this table — keep NA
  ) %>%
  left_join(coloc_locus_scored, by = c("exposure","outcome")) %>%
  mutate(
    robustness_score = case_when(
      Robustness %in% c("Very high","Very robust") ~ 3L,
      Robustness %in% c("High","Robust")          ~ 2L,
      Robustness %in% c("Moderate")               ~ 1L,
      TRUE                                        ~ 0L
    ),
    evidence_score = robustness_score + coloc_score,
    evidence_tier = case_when(
      evidence_score >= 5 ~ "Top-tier causal + shared locus",
      evidence_score >= 3 ~ "Robust causal / partial locus support",
      evidence_score >= 1 ~ "Suggestive",
      TRUE                ~ "Weak"
    )
  )


datatable(
  robust_with_coloc,
  extensions = c("Scroller"),
  options = list(
    scrollY = 400,
    scrollX = TRUE,
    scroller = TRUE,
    pageLength = 25
  ),
  rownames = FALSE
)
```

# 16. Reduction of SNPs

The harmonized SNP × trait matrix is reduced using variability-based filtering to retain the most genetically informative variants for machine-learning analysis. SNPs are ranked by cross-trait effect size standard deviation, capturing pleiotropic signal strength and multi-trait genetic structure, and the top variants are standardized to produce a computationally efficient Elastic Net input matrix.

```{r SNPreduction, echo=TRUE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=TRUE}


###############################################
# SNP REDUCTION — Variability-Based Filtering #
# Applied to FINAL harmonised SNP × trait matrix
###############################################

#------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load final clean Elastic Net input matrix
#------------------------------------------------
# Rows = SNPs
# Columns = GWAS traits
# Already harmonised, ordered, and NA-free

X <- readRDS("X_elastic_net.rds")


#------------------------------------------------
# 2. Compute genetic variability per SNP
#------------------------------------------------
# Standard deviation across traits captures:
#  - multi-trait pleiotropic structure
#  - strength of genetic signal
#  - informative SNPs for Elastic Net

snp_sd <- apply(X, 1, sd)

# Optional sanity check
summary(snp_sd)


#------------------------------------------------
# 3. Choose number of SNPs to retain
#------------------------------------------------
# Typical ranges in large-scale GWAS ML:
#  - 50k  (fast, conservative)
#  - 100k–200k (balanced, recommended)
#  - >200k (max signal, slower)

N <- 150000


#------------------------------------------------
# 4. Rank SNPs by information content
#------------------------------------------------
# Highest SD = strongest multi-trait variation

top_idx <- order(snp_sd, decreasing = TRUE)[1:N]


#------------------------------------------------
# 5. Subset SNP matrix to top informative variants
#------------------------------------------------

X_reduced <- X[top_idx, ]


#------------------------------------------------
# 6. Re-standardize predictors for Elastic Net
#------------------------------------------------
# (critical for regularization stability)

X_reduced <- scale(X_reduced)


#------------------------------------------------
# 7. Final dimension check
#------------------------------------------------
# Should be: N SNPs × number of traits

dim(X_reduced)


#------------------------------------------------
# 8. Save reduced matrix for modelling
#------------------------------------------------

saveRDS(X_reduced, "X_elastic_net_reduced_sd.rds")

cat("✅ SNP reduction complete — retained", N, "most informative variants\n")


```




# 17. Baseline predictor screening using SNP-level effect size correlations with aging outcomes

Shared genetic architecture between biological predictors and aging-related outcomes is assessed by computing SNP-level effect size correlations across the reduced variant set. Predictors are ranked by correlation strength to identify traits exhibiting the strongest pleiotropic alignment with each aging outcome.

```{r Baseline_Traits, echo=TRUE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=TRUE}

############################################################
#     Genetic correlation screening using SNP-level effects
#     (pleiotropy proxy across biological systems)
############################################################

# INPUT:
# X_reduced = SNP × trait effect matrix
# Rows      = SNPs
# Columns   = predictors + outcomes
# Already harmonised, ordered, standardized

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

############################################################
# 0. Define outcomes and predictors
############################################################

# Aging outcomes (targets)
outcomes <- c(
  "Healthspan",
  "Parental_lifespan",
  "Usual_walking_pace"
)

# Everything else is a predictor
predictors <- setdiff(colnames(X_reduced), outcomes)

############################################################
# 1. Function to compute SNP-level genetic correlations
############################################################
# For each predictor:
#   cor( beta_SNP,predictor , beta_SNP,outcome )

run_trait_correlation <- function(outcome_name) {

  y <- X_reduced[, outcome_name]

  cor_results <- lapply(predictors, function(tr) {

    x <- X_reduced[, tr]

    ct <- cor.test(x, y)

    data.frame(
      Predictor   = tr,
      Correlation = unname(ct$estimate),
      P_value     = ct$p.value,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })

  bind_rows(cor_results) %>%
    arrange(desc(abs(Correlation)))
}

############################################################
# 2. Run correlations for each aging outcome
############################################################

cor_results_all <- list()

cor_results_all[["Healthspan"]]         <- run_trait_correlation("Healthspan")
cor_results_all[["Parental_lifespan"]]  <- run_trait_correlation("Parental_lifespan")
cor_results_all[["Usual_walking_pace"]] <- run_trait_correlation("Usual_walking_pace")

############################################################
# 3. Helper to print collapsible result blocks (R Markdown)
############################################################

show_results_block <- function(df, outcome_label) {

  cat("\n\n<details>\n")
  cat("<summary><strong>", outcome_label, 
      " — SNP-level genetic correlation screening</strong></summary>\n\n")

  # --------------------------------------------------------
  # Ranked correlation table
  # --------------------------------------------------------

  print(
    kbl(df, digits = 5) %>%
      kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) %>%
      scroll_box(height = "400px")
  )

  # --------------------------------------------------------
  # Strongest genetically aligned predictor
  # --------------------------------------------------------

  best_trait <- df$Predictor[1]

  cat("\n\n**Top genetically aligned predictor:** ", best_trait, "\n\n")

  # --------------------------------------------------------
  # Visualization
  # --------------------------------------------------------

  print(
    ggplot(df, aes(x = reorder(Predictor, Correlation),
                   y = Correlation)) +
      geom_col() +
      coord_flip() +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
      labs(
        title = paste("SNP-level genetic correlation with", outcome_label),
        x = "Predictor trait",
        y = "Correlation (β_predictor vs β_outcome)"
      )
  )

  cat("\n</details>\n")
}

############################################################
# 4. Display collapsible results (one per outcome)
############################################################

show_results_block(
  cor_results_all[["Healthspan"]],
  "Healthspan"
)

show_results_block(
  cor_results_all[["Parental_lifespan"]],
  "Parental lifespan"
)

show_results_block(
  cor_results_all[["Usual_walking_pace"]],
  "Usual walking pace"
)
```

# 18. Baseline predictor screening using univariate SNP-level regression with aging outcomes

Each predictor’s SNP-level effects are regressed against aging outcome effects to quantify directional influence and explained variance. This provides a complementary measure of pleiotropic contribution strength and prioritizes predictors with the greatest genetic impact on aging traits.

```{r Baseline_Traits2, echo=TRUE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=TRUE}

############################################################
#     Baseline predictor screening using SNP-level regression
#     (pleiotropy strength + variance explained)
############################################################

# INPUT:
# X_reduced = SNP × trait effect matrix
# Rows      = SNPs
# Columns   = predictors + outcomes
# Already harmonised, ordered, standardized

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

############################################################
# 0. Define outcomes and predictors
############################################################

outcomes <- c(
  "Healthspan",
  "Parental_lifespan",
  "Usual_walking_pace"
)

predictors <- setdiff(colnames(X_reduced), outcomes)

############################################################
# 1. Function to run univariate regression for one outcome
############################################################

run_univariate_regression <- function(outcome_name) {

  y <- X_reduced[, outcome_name]

  reg_results <- lapply(predictors, function(pred) {

    x <- X_reduced[, pred]

    df <- data.frame(
      outcome   = y,
      predictor = x
    )

    fit <- lm(outcome ~ predictor, data = df)
    s   <- summary(fit)

    data.frame(
      Predictor = pred,
      Beta      = coef(fit)[2],
      P_value   = s$coefficients[2, 4],
      R2        = s$r.squared,
      Direction = ifelse(coef(fit)[2] > 0, "Positive", "Negative"),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })

  bind_rows(reg_results) %>%
    arrange(desc(R2))
}

############################################################
# 2. Run regressions for each aging outcome
############################################################

reg_results_all <- list()

reg_results_all[["Healthspan"]]         <- run_univariate_regression("Healthspan")
reg_results_all[["Parental_lifespan"]]  <- run_univariate_regression("Parental_lifespan")
reg_results_all[["Usual_walking_pace"]] <- run_univariate_regression("Usual_walking_pace")

############################################################
# 3. Helper to print collapsible blocks (R Markdown)
############################################################

show_regression_block <- function(df, outcome_label) {

  cat("\n<details>\n")
  cat("<summary><strong>", outcome_label,
      " — Univariate SNP-level regression screening</strong></summary>\n\n")

  # --------------------------------------------------------
  # Ranked regression table
  # --------------------------------------------------------

  print(
    kbl(
      df,
      digits = 5,
      caption = paste("Univariate genetic regression: predictors →", outcome_label)
    ) %>%
      kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) %>%
      scroll_box(height = "400px")
  )

  # --------------------------------------------------------
  # Best baseline predictor
  # --------------------------------------------------------

  best_trait <- df$Predictor[1]

  cat("\n\n**Best baseline predictor (highest R²):** ", best_trait, "\n\n")

  # --------------------------------------------------------
  # Visualization
  # --------------------------------------------------------

  print(
    ggplot(df, aes(x = reorder(Predictor, R2), y = R2)) +
      geom_col() +
      coord_flip() +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
      labs(
        title = paste("Explained SNP-level variance for", outcome_label),
        x = "Predictor trait",
        y = "R² (variance explained)"
      )
  )

  cat("\n</details>\n\n")
}

############################################################
# 4. Display collapsible results (one per outcome)
############################################################

show_regression_block(
  reg_results_all[["Healthspan"]],
  "Healthspan"
)

show_regression_block(
  reg_results_all[["Parental_lifespan"]],
  "Parental lifespan"
)

show_regression_block(
  reg_results_all[["Usual_walking_pace"]],
  "Usual walking pace"
)

```


# 19. Overlap of Top Predictors Across Screening Methods (per outcome) 

Results from correlation-based and regression-based screening are integrated to identify predictors consistently prioritized across both approaches. Overlap visualization and direction consistency analyses highlight robust genetic contributors to aging outcomes supported by multiple pleiotropic metrics.

```{r BaselinePA_Traits3, echo=TRUE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=TRUE}


# Overlap of Top Predictors Across Screening Methods (per outcome)

############################################################
# Goal:
# For each aging outcome:
#   Compare top predictors identified by:
#     • correlation screening
#     • univariate regression screening
#   using a Venn diagram and direction consistency check
############################################################

library(dplyr)
library(VennDiagram)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(grid)

############################################################
# Outcomes used in baseline screening
############################################################

outcomes <- c(
  "Healthspan",
  "Parental_lifespan",
  "Usual_walking_pace"
)

############################################################
# Loop over outcomes
############################################################

for (out in outcomes) {

  cat("\n<details>\n")
  cat(paste0("<summary><b>", out, " — Overlap of top predictors across methods</b></summary>\n\n"))

  ##########################################################
  # Retrieve correlation + regression tables for this outcome
  # (from Section 17 & 18 results you generated)
  ##########################################################

  cor_df_out <- cor_results_all[[out]]   # you created these per outcome
  reg_df_out <- reg_results_all[[out]]

  ##########################################################
  # Top 10 by absolute correlation
  ##########################################################

  top10_cor <- cor_df_out %>%
    mutate(abs_cor = abs(Correlation)) %>%
    arrange(desc(abs_cor)) %>%
    slice(1:10) %>%
    pull(Predictor)

  ##########################################################
  # Top 10 by explained variance (R²)
  ##########################################################

  top10_r2 <- reg_df_out %>%
    arrange(desc(R2)) %>%
    slice(1:10) %>%
    pull(Predictor)

  ##########################################################
  # Intersection
  ##########################################################

  intersect_traits <- intersect(top10_cor, top10_r2)

  ##########################################################
  # Venn diagram
  ##########################################################

  venn.plot <- draw.pairwise.venn(
    area1 = length(top10_cor),
    area2 = length(top10_r2),
    cross.area = length(intersect_traits),
    category = c("Correlation", "Univariate R²"),
    fill = c("#1f77b4", "#ff7f0e"),
    alpha = 0.5,
    cex = 1.3,
    cat.cex = 1.3
  )

  grid.draw(venn.plot)

  ##########################################################
  # Direction consistency table
  ##########################################################

  direction_df <- data.frame(
    Predictor = intersect_traits,
    Correlation = cor_df_out$Correlation[
      match(intersect_traits, cor_df_out$Predictor)
    ],
    Beta = reg_df_out$Beta[
      match(intersect_traits, reg_df_out$Predictor)
    ],
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  direction_df$Sign_correlation <- ifelse(direction_df$Correlation > 0, "Positive", "Negative")
  direction_df$Sign_regression  <- ifelse(direction_df$Beta > 0, "Positive", "Negative")

  direction_df$Consistent_direction <-
    direction_df$Sign_correlation == direction_df$Sign_regression

  ##########################################################
  # Display
  ##########################################################

  kbl(
    direction_df,
    digits = 4,
    caption = paste("Direction consistency of overlapping predictors for", out)
  ) %>%
    kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

  ##########################################################
  # Quick interpretation
  ##########################################################

  cat("\n")
  cat("Overlapping predictors:", length(intersect_traits), "\n")
  cat(
    "Consistent direction:",
    sum(direction_df$Consistent_direction),
    "/", nrow(direction_df), "\n\n"
  )

  cat("</details>\n\n")
}



rm(pa_lookup, X, snp_sd, snps_ref, X_reduced)
gc(TRUE)
```

# 20. Selection of Baseline Model Traits using LDSC Automation 

```{r LDSC, echo=TRUE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=FALSE}


#############################################
### LDSC AUTOMATION SCRIPT FOR 27 PA TRAITS
### Runs in RStudio, calls Python LDSC
#############################################

library(data.table)
library(stringr)

### ---- 1. Define paths ---- ###
ldsc_path <- "C:/ldsc/"   # folder where ldsc.py and munge_sumstats.py are
ref_ld <- file.path(ldsc_path, "eur_w_ld_chr")
hm3 <- file.path(ldsc_path, "w_hm3.snplist")

pa_folder <- "C:/Users/75118/Desktop/UEA/Proyecto 1/data/"
bmd_file  <- "C:/Users/75118/Desktop/UEA/Proyecto 1/data outcome/Biobank2-British-Bmd-As-C-Gwas-SumStats.txt"

out_folder <- "C:/Users/75118/Desktop/UEA/Proyecto 1/ldsc_results/"
dir.create(out_folder, showWarnings = FALSE)

### ---- 2. List all PA GWAS files ---- ###
pa_files <- list.files(pa_folder, pattern = "\\.tsv$", full.names = TRUE)

### ---- 3. MUNGE BMD FILE ---- ###
bmd_munged <- file.path(out_folder, "BMD.sumstats.gz")

cmd_munge_bmd <- paste(
  "python", file.path(ldsc_path, "munge_sumstats.py"),
  "--sumstats", shQuote(bmd_file),
  "--merge-alleles", shQuote(hm3),
  "--out", shQuote(file.path(out_folder, "BMD"))
)

system(cmd_munge_bmd)
cat("BMD munge done.\n")


### ---- 4. Loop over PA traits: munge + LDSC ---- ###

results <- data.frame(
  trait = character(),
  rg = numeric(),
  se = numeric(),
  p = numeric(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

for (f in pa_files) {

  trait_name <- str_replace(basename(f), "_buildGRCh37.tsv", "")
  cat("Processing:", trait_name, "\n")

  ### -- 4A. Munge PA file -- ###
  munged_out <- file.path(out_folder, paste0(trait_name))
  
  cmd_munge <- paste(
    "python", file.path(ldsc_path, "munge_sumstats.py"),
    "--sumstats", shQuote(f),
    "--merge-alleles", shQuote(hm3),
    "--out", shQuote(munged_out)
  )
  system(cmd_munge)

  ### -- 4B. Run LDSC -- ###
  pa_sumstats <- paste0(munged_out, ".sumstats.gz")
  ldsc_out <- file.path(out_folder, paste0(trait_name, "_vs_BMD"))

  cmd_ldsc <- paste(
    "python", file.path(ldsc_path, "ldsc.py"),
    "--rg", paste0(pa_sumstats, ",", bmd_munged),
    "--ref-ld-chr", shQuote(ref_ld),
    "--w-ld-chr", shQuote(ref_ld),
    "--out", shQuote(ldsc_out)
  )
  system(cmd_ldsc)

  ### -- 4C. Extract rg, SE, p-value from LDSC output -- ###
  log_file <- paste0(ldsc_out, ".log")
  log_text <- readLines(log_file)

  rg_line <- log_text[grepl("Genetic correlation:", log_text)]
  
  # Example line: "Genetic correlation: -0.2483 (0.062) p = 3e-05"
  rg_val <- sub(".*: (.*) \\(.*", "\\1", rg_line)
  se_val <- sub(".*\\((.*)\\).*", "\\1", rg_line)
  p_val  <- sub(".*p = (.*)", "\\1", rg_line)

  results <- rbind(results,
                   data.frame(trait = trait_name,
                              rg = as.numeric(rg_val),
                              se = as.numeric(se_val),
                              p = as.numeric(p_val)))
}

### ---- 5. Save results ---- ###
write.csv(results, file.path(out_folder, "genetic_correlations_PA_vs_BMD.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

cat("DONE! Results saved.\n")
```
